'''Interpol''' is an American [[Rock music|rock]] band from [[Manhattan]], New York.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://juiceonline.com/julian-plenti-escape-from-manhattan/ |title=Julian Plenti: Escape From Manhattan? |last=Liew |first=Ben |date=October 23, 2009 |website=Juice |access-date=August 22, 2018}}</ref><ref name="age bio">{{cite web|url=http://www.theage.com.au/news/music/interpols-apart/2008/02/21/1203467263110.html?page=fullpage#contentSwap1|title=Interpol's apart|last=Mathieson|first=Craig|date= February 22, 2008| work = [[The Age]]|access-date= December 13, 2009}}</ref> Formed in 1997, their original line-up consisted of [[Paul Banks (American singer)|Paul Banks]] (lead vocals, rhythm guitar), [[Daniel Kessler (guitarist)|Daniel Kessler]] (lead guitar, backing vocals), [[Carlos Dengler]] (bass guitar, keyboards), and [[Greg Drudy]] (drums). Drudy left the band in 2000 and was replaced by [[Sam Fogarino]]. Dengler left to pursue other projects in 2010, with Banks taking on the additional in-studio role of bassist instead of hiring a new one.

Having first performed at [[Luna Lounge]] alongside peers such as [[the Strokes]], [[Longwave (band)|Longwave]], [[The National (band)|the National]], and [[Stellastarr]], Interpol is one of the bands associated with the [[Music of New York City|New York indie music scene]] and one of several groups that emerged from the [[post-punk revival]] of the 2000s.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/whats-on/music-nightlife-news/interpol-albert-hall-manchester-tickets-12495269 |title=Interpol announce Manchester show on Turn On The Bright Lights anniversary tour |last=Heward |first=Emily |newspaper=[[Manchester Evening News]] |publication-date=January 23, 2017 |access-date=January 24, 2017}}</ref> The band's sound is generally a mix of [[staccato]] bass and rhythmic, harmonized guitar with a snare-heavy mix, drawing comparisons to post-punk bands such as [[Joy Division]], [[Television (band)|Television]] and [[the Chameleons]],<ref>Everly, David. "Our Love to Admire". ''[[Q (magazine)|Q]]'', July 2007.</ref> and also to [[Echo & the Bunnymen]] and [[Siouxsie and the Banshees]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Will|last=Hodgkinson|url=https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/interpol-interview-20th-anniversary-s0x7br82g|title=Interpol: misery loves a comeback|work=The Times|date=9 July 2022|access-date=19 July 2022|quote=Interpol, with their sharp suits, poetic air of gothic otherness and songs recalling the post-punk iciness of Echo & the Bunnymen and Siouxsie and the Banshees, were easier to romanticise than most.|archive-date=July 9, 2022|archive-url=https://archive.today/20220709005907/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/interpol-interview-20th-anniversary-s0x7br82g|url-status=bot: unknown}}</ref> The band has no primary [[songwriter]], with each member contributing to composition.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Downs|first1=Gordon|title=An interview with INTERPOL|url=http://www.imposemagazine.com/features/an-interview-with-interpol|access-date=May 27, 2017|work=[[Impose (magazine)|Impose]]|date=July 30, 2007}}</ref>

Interpol's first full-length album ''[[Turn On the Bright Lights]]'' (2002) was critically acclaimed, making it to No. 10 on ''[[NME]]''{{'s}} list of the top albums of the year<ref>{{cite web|title=NME Albums of the Year 2002 |work=[[NME]] |url=https://www.nme.com/reviews/albums/oftheyear |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080413112951/http://www.nme.com/reviews/albums/oftheyear |archive-date=April 13, 2008}}</ref> and No. 1 on [[Pitchfork Media]]'s list of the top 50 albums of the year.<ref>{{cite web|title=Top 50 Albums of 2002 |publisher=[[Pitchfork Media]] |date=January 1, 2003 |url=http://www.pitchforkmedia.com/article/feature/38222-staff-list-top-50-albums-of-2002/page_5 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080905060937/http://www.pitchforkmedia.com/article/feature/38222-staff-list-top-50-albums-of-2002/page_5 |archive-date=September 5, 2008}}</ref> Subsequent records ''[[Antics (album)|Antics]]'' (2004) and ''[[Our Love to Admire]]'' (2007) brought greater critical and commercial success. The band released its fourth full-length album, [[Interpol (album)|''Interpol'']], in September 2010, then went on hiatus while they focused on other projects.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.gigwise.com/news/66381/Interpol-We-Need-A-Big-Break-Before-Next-Album|title=Interpol: We Need A Big Break Before Next Album : Drummer Sam Fogarino says...|work=Gigwise.com|access-date=September 5, 2014}}</ref> Their fifth studio album, ''[[El Pintor]]'', was released in September 2014. The band embarked on an anniversary tour for ''Turn On the Bright Lights'' in 2017, performing the album live in its entirety. The band's sixth studio album, ''[[Marauder (Interpol album)|Marauder]]'', was released in August 2018, and their seventh, ''[[The Other Side of Make-Believe]]'', in July 2022. In 2024, the band embarked on a 20th anniversary tour for ''Antics'', where the album was performed in its entirety.

==History==
===Formation and early releases (1997–2001)===
The band was formed by Kessler and Drudy. Kessler had "been looking to put a band together for a while" when he met Drudy. Kessler "had a very hard time finding musicians to play with—musicians at all, really."<ref name="Pitchfork" /> Kessler met Dengler in a philosophy class at [[New York University]] and asked him if he played an instrument. Later, Kessler ran into Banks (whom he had first met in France) in New York City's [[East Village, Manhattan|East Village]], and the pair discussed collaborating. Banks admitted that he and Dengler "butted heads" early on in the band's history, but told ''[[Spin (magazine)|Spin]]'' that now the two are "really tight, in a spiritual way".<ref name="Night">Raftery, Brian. "Night Falls on Manhattan". ''[[Spin (magazine)|Spin]]''. April 2005.</ref> The band had trouble choosing a name at first. "I got to the point where I was like, 'Guys, we're getting decent crowds, but like... we don't have a name so no one knows who to go see again,'" Kessler said.<ref name="Pitchfork">{{cite web |title = Interview: Interpol |publisher = [[Pitchfork Media]] |date = February 1, 2003 |access-date = February 7, 2009 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080309071525/http://www.pitchforkmedia.com/article/feature/31388-interview-interpol |archive-date= March 9, 2008 |url= http://www.pitchforkmedia.com/article/feature/31388-interview-interpol}}</ref> Furthermore, the band considered the names Las Armas<ref name="Pitchfork" /> and The French Letters before adopting Interpol.

In 2000, after releasing the ''[[Fukd ID 3|Fukd ID No.&nbsp;3]]'' [[extended play|extended-play]] album, Drudy left the band to focus on [[Hot Cross]] and his label [[Level Plane Records]]. Kessler recruited Fogarino, who worked at a local vintage clothing store and at the time considered retiring from music, to replace Drudy.<ref name="Night" /> While a member of Interpol, Drudy was also a member of seminal first-wave [[screamo]] act [[Saetia]].

===Signing with Matador Records, ''Turn On the Bright Lights'' and ''Antics'' (2002–2005)===
[[File:Interpol Concert in Las Vegas, September 19, 2005-4.jpg|thumb|right|Interpol performing in [[Las Vegas]], 2005]]
After self-releasing several EPs between 1998 and 2001, the band signed with [[Matador Records]], a member of the independent [[Beggars Group]], in early 2002. The first release, an EP titled simply [[Interpol EP|''Interpol'']], containing re-recorded versions of "PDA" and "NYC", was released in June 2002. ''[[Turn On the Bright Lights]]'' was released on August 19, 2002. Recorded at Tarquin Studios in [[Bridgeport, Connecticut]], the album's sound drew comparisons to [[post-punk]] groups of the early 1980s and late 1970s, particularly [[Joy Division]], [[Echo and the Bunnymen]] and [[the Smiths]].<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/albumreviews/turn-on-the-bright-lights-20020814 |title=Interpol: ''Turn On The Bright Lights'' |first=Rob |last=Sheffield |date=August 14, 2002 |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |access-date=September 11, 2011 |archive-date=October 27, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111027192756/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/albumreviews/turn-on-the-bright-lights-20020814 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The record was a slow-building success, selling 300,000 copies by 2004.<ref name="Night" />

The band regrouped in late 2003 to begin sessions for the follow-up album, again decamping to Tarquin Studios to record. The band released its second album ''[[Antics (album)|Antics]]'' on September 27, 2004. The album sold 350,000 copies in its first four months of release.<ref name="Night" /> The record also saw the band earn its first UK Top 40 hits with "[[Slow Hands (Interpol song)|Slow Hands]]", "[[Evil (Interpol song)|Evil]]" and "[[C'mere]]" charting at No.&nbsp;36, No.&nbsp;18 and No.&nbsp;19, respectively.<ref name="British Hit Singles & Albums">{{cite book| first= David| last= Roberts| year= 2006| title= British Hit Singles & Albums| edition= 19th| publisher= [[Guinness World Records Limited]] | location= London| isbn= 1-904994-10-5| page= 270}}</ref> The album eventually reached Gold status in the UK, and later in the US.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.riaa.com/goldandplatinumdata.php?table=SEARCH_RESULTS&artist=Interpol&format=ALBUM&go=Search&perPage=50 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130104155006/http://www.riaa.com/goldandplatinumdata.php?table=SEARCH_RESULTS&artist=Interpol&format=ALBUM&go=Search&perPage=50 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 4, 2013 |title=Recording Industry Association of America |publisher=RIAA |access-date=July 6, 2011 }}</ref>

The band toured again after the release of the album, playing more dates than ever before and at bigger venues. The ''Antics'' tour stretched on for almost 18 months, including playing as [[undercard]]s for [[U2]] and [[the Cure]], and the band expressed feelings of exhaustion to [[BBC Radio 1]] DJ [[Zane Lowe]] at a concert in [[City of Sunderland|Sunderland]]. The band took three months off after touring finished. Whilst on the road, the band had also released the one-off track "Direction", written for the official [[soundtrack]] to [[HBO]]'s ''[[Six Feet Under (TV series)|Six Feet Under]]'', ''[[Six Feet Under, Vol. 2: Everything Ends]]''.

===Move to Capitol Records and ''Our Love to Admire'' (2006–2008)===
[[File:Interpol (band).jpg|thumb|left|Interpol performing at the Super Bock Super Rock Festival in [[Lisbon]], 2007]]
In late March 2006, Fogarino confirmed that the band were back in the studio working on new material. In an interview with [[Pitchfork Media]], Fogarino stated "[the process is] moving right along where I think it should...we're all pretty much on fire about it".<ref>{{cite web |author=Solarski, Matthew|title=Interpol Drummer Talks Photos, Stipe, Interscope |url=http://www.pitchforkmedia.com/article/news/36038-interpol-drummer-talks-photos-stipe-interscope |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080307163103/http://www.pitchforkmedia.com/article/news/36038-interpol-drummer-talks-photos-stipe-interscope |publisher= [[Pitchfork Media]] |archive-date= March 7, 2008 |date= March 30, 2006 |access-date= May 14, 2009}}</ref> Fogarino also dispelled rumors that the band had signed to major label [[Interscope Records|Interscope]], but also confirmed that they would be leaving Matador in search of a new label. An update to their website in June confirmed that the band had been working on the follow-up since the turn of the year, but did not confirm a name for the album or comment on the mounting speculation that they were imminently to sign to a major label. On August 14, it was widely reported that Interpol had signed for [[Capitol Records]], a fact confirmed by Matador on September 1 in a press release on their website.

''[[Our Love to Admire]]'' was released in July 2007. The album represents a departure for the band, being both the first record they have recorded in New York City (at [[Magic Shop (recording studio)|The Magic Shop]] and [[Electric Lady Studios]]), and the first time they have included keyboards in the arrangements from the start of the songwriting process. The band intended to tour behind the album extensively, beginning with the summer festival circuit throughout the United States and Europe. In August, Interpol headlined one of the days of the [[Lollapalooza]] music festival in Chicago.
{{clear}}

===Return to Matador, ''Interpol'' and departure of Carlos Dengler (2009–2011)===
[[File:Interpol rh balt.JPG|thumb|right|Interpol playing at [[Rams Head Live!]], [[Baltimore]], July 25, 2010]]
On March 6, 2009, the band announced on its website that it was working on songs for a fourth album.<ref name="official">{{Official website|http://www.interpolnyc.com/}}</ref> The album was recorded in [[Electric Lady Studios]] during spring 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pitchfork.com/news/37161-new-interpol-album-coming-next-year/ |title=New Interpol Album Coming Next Year |date=November 19, 2009 |publisher=[[Pitchfork Media]] |access-date= July 6, 2011}}</ref> In an interview, Fogarino referred to the album as having gone back to the original sound of ''Turn On the Bright Lights''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/articles/2009/11/interpol-drummer-explains-new-album-out-in-early-2.html |title=Sam Fogarino Talks New Interpol Album, Courtney Love |work=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]] |access-date=July 6, 2011 |archive-date=February 2, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200202212639/https://www.pastemagazine.com/articles/2009/11/interpol-drummer-explains-new-album-out-in-early-2.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> It was later claimed by Banks that it would not sound anything like their debut album and that there is some very "classical stuff going on" with it.<ref>{{cite web|author= Rogers, Georgie |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/6music/news/20091217_interpol.shtml |title=Interpol Go Orchestral – Paul Banks Gives Us the Lowdown on Their 'Classical' Fourth Album |publisher=[[BBC Radio 6 Music]] |date= December 17, 2009 |access-date= March 9, 2013}}</ref> No news about the album surfaced until late April when the band sent an email directing users to a free download of "Lights", the first officially released song. Citing management changes at the label, the band left Capitol Records prior to the album's release, signing again with [[Matador Records]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Partridge|first=Kenneth|title=Interpol Have No Regrets About Capitol Stint|url=http://www.spinner.com/2010/08/06/interpol-capitol-matador-new-album/|work=Spinner.com|publisher=AOL|access-date=February 21, 2013|archive-date=September 15, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190915015936/http://www.spinner.com/2010/08/06/interpol-capitol-matador-new-album|url-status=dead}}</ref> On June 22, 2010, a promotional video for "Lights", directed by [[Charlie White (artist)|Charlie White]] and featuring [[Lola Blanc]], was made available for free download on the band's official website.

The [[Interpol (album)|band's fourth album]] (self-titled) was officially released on September 7, 2010.<ref>{{dead link|date=March 2013}} {{cite magazine |url=https://consequence.net/2010/06/04/interpol-finds-new-bassist-titles-new-album/ |title=Interpol Finds New Bassist, Titles New Album |magazine=[[Consequence of Sound]] |date=June 4, 2010 |access-date=July 6, 2011 }}{{Dead link|date=December 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> It was Dengler's last effort with Interpol. In an announcement on the band's website on May 9, 2010, it was revealed that he had left the band sometime after the album's completion. When the remaining members toured in support, he was replaced by multiple players, including [[David Pajo]] (formerly of [[Slint]] and many other bands) on bass, and [[Brandon Curtis]] of [[The Secret Machines]] on keyboards and vocals.<ref name="ofnews">{{cite web|url=http://www.interpolnyc.com/news.html |title=Interpol |date=May 9, 2010 |publisher=Interpol |access-date=May 9, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100605074840/http://www.interpolnyc.com/news.html |archive-date=June 5, 2010}}</ref> The album was released on Matador Records in the US, and on [[Cooperative Music]] for Europe, Australia and Japan.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cooperative-music-france.com/flyer/interpolsignesurcoop.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100618072250/http://www.cooperative-music-france.com/flyer/interpolsignesurcoop.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 18, 2010 |title=Interpol signe chez Cooperative Music |trans-title=Interpol Signs with Cooperative Music |language=fr |publisher=Cooperative-music-france.com |access-date=July 6, 2011 }}</ref> In February 2011, Pajo announced that he was no longer touring with Interpol, in order to dedicate more time to his family. Pajo was subsequently replaced by Brad Truax.<ref name="ofnews" />

The band was announced as the opener for the third and fourth legs of [[U2]]'s [[U2 360° Tour|360° Tour]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pitchfork.com/news/37984-interpol-to-tour-with-u2/ |title=Interpol to Tour With U2 |publisher=[[Pitchfork Media]] |date= February 22, 2010 |access-date= July 6, 2011}}</ref> and subsequently the band announced eighteen US shows to take place over the third leg of U2's 360° Tour, but only three of them went ahead after Bono's back injury cancelled U2's entire third leg. The band toured the UK and Ireland in November and December 2010.{{citation needed|date=October 2021}} The band opened for U2 on their rescheduled tour date at [[Soldier Field]] in [[Chicago]], [[Illinois]], on July 5, 2011, and remained on U2's 360° Tour for the remainder of the summer.

=== Brief hiatus and ''El Pintor'' (2012–2015) ===
[[File:El Pintor Interpol.jpg|thumb|left|Interpol performing in 2015 during their El Pintor Tour]]
After the band's appearance at Reading and Leeds in 2011, Fogarino was interviewed.<ref name="gigwisebreak">{{cite web |publisher=Gigwise Official Website |url=http://www.gigwise.com/news/66381/Interpol-We-Need-A-Big-Break-Before-Next-Album |title=Interpol: We Need A Big Break Before Next Album |date= August 31, 2011}}</ref> He said, "[w]e need a big break. Interpol needs it. We need to recoup and go on a proper hiatus." He stated that the remaining members of the band would be pursuing separate projects, one of which included a [[Banks (album)|second solo album]] by Paul Banks.{{citation needed|date=October 2021}} A deluxe edition of the band's first album, ''Turn on the Bright Lights'' was released on December 4, 2012, to mark the album's ten-year anniversary. It includes previously hard-to-find tracks, including "Get The Girls" and "Cubed".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/news/interpol/66370 |title=Interpol's 'Turn On The Bright Lights' gets 10th anniversary reissue | work = [[NME]] |date=September 28, 2012 |access-date= December 12, 2012}}</ref>

The band announced on June 5, 2014, that their fifth studio album, entitled ''[[El Pintor]]'', would be released on September 9, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.interpolnyc.com/news.html |title=Interpol : ''El Pintor'' |publisher=Interpolnyc.com |access-date=September 5, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100605074840/http://www.interpolnyc.com/news.html |archive-date=June 5, 2010}}</ref> This album's name was derived as an anagram by Paul Banks who created the name while thinking of new design concepts for merchandise.<ref>Daly, Rhian. "Albums of the Year: 49 - Interpol: "El Pintor"." ''NME - New Musical Express'' November 29, 2014: 27. ''ProQuest.'' Web. February 15, 2016</ref> It was the band's first album since the departure of bassist Carlos Dengler, with Paul Banks taking over bass duties for the first time as well as touring member Brandon Curtis taking over keyboard duties on nine of the ten album tracks.<ref>{{cite magazine | url=https://consequence.net/2014/06/interpol-announce-new-album-el-pintor-due-out-in-september/ | title=Interpol announce new album, El Pintor, due out in September | magazine=[[Consequence of Sound]] | date=June 5, 2014 | access-date=June 5, 2014 | author=Young, Alex}}</ref>

To promote the album, Interpol embarked a world tour which started in June 2014. While on tour in November, the band were one of the many caught in the [[November 2014 North American cold wave|heavy snow storms]] in [[Buffalo, New York]]. The band's tour bus was unable to move and they were stuck under the snow for more than 50 hours. Three shows, two in Canada and one in Boston, were postponed as a result.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Geslani|first1=Michelle|title=Interpol have been stranded on Buffalo highway for 50 hours due to record-breaking snowstorm|url=https://consequence.net/2014/11/interpol-have-been-stranded-on-buffalo-highway-for-30-hours-due-to-record-breaking-snowstorm/|access-date=June 16, 2015|work=Consequence of Sound|date=November 19, 2014}}</ref> Touring for ''El Pintor'' culminated in a performance at the 2015 [[Electric Picnic]] festival.

''El Pintor'' was followed up by a remix album, ''El Pintor Remixes'', which featured electronic musicians such as [[Panda Bear (musician)|Panda Bear]], [[Factory Floor]] and [[The Field (musician)|The Field]].<ref>{{cite web|title=INTERPOL ANNOUNCE REMIX LP, 'EL PINTOR REMIXES'|date=March 10, 2016 |url=https://diymag.com/2016/03/10/interpol-announce-remix-lp-el-pintor-remixes|publisher=DIY}}</ref>

=== ''Marauder'' and ''A Fine Mess'' (2016–2019) ===
[[File:Primavera19 -98 (48986113281).jpg|thumb|right|Interpol performing at [[Primavera Sound]] in 2019]]
In September 2016, Paul Banks revealed in an interview on [[Beats 1]] that Interpol would resume writing in the fall.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://itunes.apple.com/ca/post/idsa.02cd07ba-746c-11e6-b331-337373bb5a40|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161101042508/https://itunes.apple.com/ca/post/idsa.02cd07ba-746c-11e6-b331-337373bb5a40|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 1, 2016|title=Watch "Will Interpol be back?! - Paul Banks of Banks & Steelz" posted by Ebro Darden on Apple Music.|website=[[iTunes]]|access-date=May 23, 2017}}</ref>  In January 2017, Interpol announced that their sixth album would be out in 2018 and that they would embark on a tour for ''Turn On the Bright Lights' '' 15th anniversary, playing the entire album front to back.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Pearce|first1=Sheldon|title=Interpol Announce Turn On the Bright Lights Anniversary Tour|url=https://pitchfork.com/news/71055-interpol-announce-turn-on-the-bright-lights-anniversary-tour/|website=Pitchfork|date=January 23, 2017 |access-date=January 23, 2017}}</ref> In between the tour and announcement of the new album, they released an EP consisting of bonus tracks from ''El Pintor''. The tracks included were "The Depths", "Malfeasance", and "What Is What".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://boomkat.com/products/el-pintor-bonus-tracks|title=El Pintor Bonus Tracks|website=Boomkat|access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref>

On May 24, 2018, ''Pitchfork'' noted that the name of the new album would be ''Marauder'' in their Guide to New Albums: Summer 2018 list.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/the-pitchfork-guide-to-new-albums-summer-2018/ |title=The Pitchfork Guide to New Albums: Summer 2018 |last1=Wicks |first1=Amanda |last2=Kim |first2=Michelle |date=May 24, 2018 |website=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180524143557/https://pitchfork.com/news/the-pitchfork-guide-to-new-albums-summer-2018/ |archive-date=May 24, 2018 |access-date=May 24, 2018 |last3=Blais-Billie |first3=Braudie |last4=Yoo |first4=Noah |last5=Bloom |first5=Madison}}</ref> In June 2018, the band held a press conference in [[Mexico City]] and announced the ''[[Marauder (Interpol album)|Marauder]]'' release date, August 24, 2018. The same day they released the first single of the album entitled "The Rover".<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/interpol-announce-new-album-marauder-share-new-song-the-rover-listen/ |title=Interpol Announce New Album Marauder, Share New Song "The Rover": Listen |last1=Kim |first1=Michelle |last2=Strauss |first2=Matthew |date=June 7, 2018 |website=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]] |access-date=April 1, 2019}}</ref> A month later Interpol released their second single from the album, "Number 10".<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://consequence.net/2018/07/interpol-number-10-marauder-new-song/ |title=Interpol share new, office-set single "Number 10": Stream |last=Colborn |first=Randall |date=July 30, 2018 |website=[[Consequence of Sound]] |access-date=April 1, 2019}}</ref> On August 23, the music video for their single "If You Really Love Nothing" was released.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/interpol-release-edgy-new-video-really-love-nothing-featuring-kristen-stewart-finn-wittrock-2370105|title=Kristen Stewart and Finn Wittrock star in Interpol's edgy new video for 'If You Really Love Nothing' - NME|date=August 23, 2018|work=NME|access-date=August 24, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref>

On January 30, 2019, Interpol released "Fine Mess", a song that was left off of ''Marauder'', as a single.<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/hear-interpols-haunting-new-song-fine-mess-786573/ |title=Hear Interpol's Haunting New Song 'Fine Mess' |last=Greene |first=Andy |date=January 30, 2019 |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |access-date=April 1, 2019}}</ref> On March 28, the band announced a new EP, ''A Fine Mess'', consisting of songs from the ''Marauder'' sessions that didn't make the final cut, with a release date of May 17, 2019. On the same day, they released the second single off the EP, "The Weekend".<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/interpol-a-fine-mess-ep-new-music-weekend-paul-banks-interview-tour-strokes-2467016 |title=Interpol tell us about their new 'A Fine Mess' EP: "This is about taking the party by the horns" |last=Trendell |first=Andrew |date=March 28, 2019 |website=[[NME]] |access-date=March 29, 2019}}</ref> On August 16, 2019, ''Our Love to Admire'' became unavailable on streaming platforms which caused some panic among fans. Lead singer Paul Banks quickly addressed the issue by reassuring fans via Twitter that the album would be returned to streaming platforms.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/bankspaulbanks/status/1162381538136383488|title=Hey gang! Thanks for the heads ups. OLTA will be back up on streaming pronto. Hang tight!|last=Banks|first=Paul|date=August 16, 2019|website=@bankspaulbanks|language=en|access-date=August 28, 2019}}</ref> On December 10, 2020, it was announced that Matador Records had finally acquired the rights to Interpol's entire catalog.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/business/9497186/deals-matador-interpol-pavement-sony-masterworks-broadway|title=The Deals: Matador Acquires Interpol & Pavement Catalog Rights, Sony Masterworks Takes On Broadway|website=Billboard.com|access-date=May 20, 2021}}</ref>

=== ''The Other Side of Make-Believe'' (2020–present) ===
[[File:Interpol in Pittsburgh 2022.jpg|alt=Landscape photo depicting Interpol playing in concert in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania|thumb|Interpol performing in Pittsburgh in 2022]]
Interpol began writing songs for a seventh studio album during the summer of 2020. The [[COVID-19 pandemic]] had impacted the way they wrote music; the band wrote in an Instagram post that they, at first, "had to use the internet to circulate ideas and collaborate remotely" before eventually being able to write music together in person at a house in the [[Catskill Mountains]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clarke |first=Patrick |date=June 17, 2021 |title=Interpol have "been working on new music since last summer" |url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/interpol-have-been-working-on-new-music-since-last-summer-2972328 |access-date=September 28, 2021 |website=[[NME]]}}</ref> They began recording the album in London during 2021 alongside producers [[Flood (producer)|Flood]] and [[Alan Moulder]], the latter of whom previously mixed ''Interpol'' (2010) and ''El Pintor'' (2014). The album's first single "[[Toni (Interpol song)|Toni]]" premiered on April 7.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Goggins |first1=Joe |title=Interpol tease first single from seventh album with clip from new video |url=https://www.rollingstone.co.uk/music/news/interpol-tease-first-single-seventh-album-clip-new-video-14382/ |access-date=April 7, 2022 |magazine=Rolling Stone |date=April 6, 2022}}</ref> ''[[The Other Side of Make-Believe]]'' and was released on July 15, 2022, along with a music video for "Gran Hotel".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Corcoran |first1=Nina |title=Interpol Announce New Album The Other Side of Make-Believe, Share Video for New Song "Toni": Watch |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/interpol-announce-new-album-the-other-side-of-make-believe-share-video-for-new-song-toni-watch/ |access-date=April 7, 2022 |work=Pitchfork |date=April 7, 2022}}</ref> 

Beginning in 2023, Chris Broome filled in for drummer Sam Fogarino, who was recovering from spinal surgery.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-23 |title=Interpol drummer drops off upcoming shows after undergoing cervical spine surgery |url=https://www.1057thepoint.com/music-news/interpol-drummer-drops-off-upcoming-shows-after-undergoing-cervical-spine-surgery/ |access-date=2025-04-23 |website=105.7 The Point |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Russell |first=Will |title=Live Report: Interpol celebrate 20 years of Antics at the 3Arena |url=https://www.hotpress.com/music/live-report-interpol-celebrate-20-years-of-antics-at-the-3arena-23058300 |access-date=2025-04-23 |website=Hotpress}}</ref>

On April 20, 2024, Interpol performed a free concert at the [[Zócalo]] in [[Mexico City]] to an estimated crowd of 160,000, the largest show of the band's career.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Cano |first=Natalia |date=2024-04-21 |title=Interpol Plays Biggest Show of Its Career in Mexico City: 5 Best Moments |url=https://www.billboard.com/lists/interpol-mexico-city-zocalo-concert-best-moments/ |access-date=2024-12-12 |magazine=Billboard |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Side projects==
In early 2007, Fogarino joined with former [[Swervedriver]] frontman [[Adam Franklin]] to form a side-project band called The Setting Suns. Since then, the duo have changed their name to [[Magnetic Morning]] and released a six-track EP on iTunes.

On August 4, 2009, Banks released his first solo record titled ''[[Julian Plenti is... Skyscraper]]'' under the assumed name Julian Plenti.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/news/interpol/44465/ |title=Interpol Man to Release Solo Album | work = [[NME]] |date= May 5, 2009 |access-date= October 15, 2011}}</ref> Although not a long departure from Interpol's sound, the album features a wider range of material, and "establishes Banks' viability as a musician outside of the context of Interpol".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/13224-julian-plenti-is-skyscraper/ |title=Julian Plenti Is... Skyscraper |author= LeMay, Matt |date= July 31, 2009 |publisher=[[Pitchfork Media]] |access-date= November 21, 2009}}</ref> The album was recorded at the Seaside Lounge in Brooklyn and at [[Electric Lady Studios]] in Manhattan. It was mixed by [[Peter Katis]] at Tarquin Studios in Connecticut. The album was released on [[Matador Records]]. He released his second solo album, ''[[Banks (Paul Banks album)|Banks]]'', on October 22, 2012, under his own name.

In 2013, Fogarino, touring Interpol member [[Brandon Curtis]], and [[Duane Denison]] formed EmptyMansions, who released their album ''snakes/vultures/sulfate'' via [[Riot House Records]] in April 2013.

In 2014, [[Daniel Kessler (guitarist)|Daniel Kessler]] formed Big Noble with sound designer Joseph Fraioli of Datach'i. They released their debut album ''First Light'' on February 2, 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/56942-interpols-daniel-kessler-launches-side-project-big-noble/ |title=Interpol's Daniel Kessler Launches Side Project Big Noble |author= Gordon, Jeremy |date= October 2, 2014 |publisher=[[Pitchfork Media]] |access-date= October 8, 2014}}</ref>

In 2016, Paul Banks released an album alongside [[Wu-Tang Clan]] member [[RZA]] under the name [[Banks & Steelz]]. The album, titled ''[[Anything But Words]]'', was released on August 26, 2016, through [[Warner Bros. Records]].<ref>{{cite magazine | url=http://www.factmag.com/2016/06/09/interpol-paul-banks-rza-banks-steelz-anything-but-words/ | title=RZA and Interpol's Paul Banks announce debut album ''Anything But Words'' | magazine=[[Fact (UK magazine)|Fact]] | date=June 9, 2016 | access-date=September 24, 2019 | author=Bowe, Miles}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://itunes.apple.com/us/album/anything-but-words/id1119641169 | title=Anything But Words by Banks & Steelz | publisher=[[iTunes|iTunes U.S.]] | access-date=July 5, 2016}}</ref>

In 2020, Paul Banks announced a new side project by the name of Muzz. The band also consists of [[Josh Kaufman (musician)|Josh Kaufman]] and [[The Walkmen|Matt Barrick]]. Their self-titled debut LP, ''[[Muzz (album)|Muzz]]'' was released on June 5, 2020, through [[Matador Records]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/muzz-muzz/ |title=Muzz Album Review|publisher=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]]|date=June 4, 2020|author=Schonfeld, Zach}}</ref>

'''Extreme''' is an American [[Rock music|rock]] band formed in [[Boston]], [[Massachusetts]], in 1985, that reached the height of their popularity in the late 1980s and early 1990s. They have released six studio albums, two EPs (in Japan) and two compilation albums since their formation. The band was one of the most successful rock acts of the early 1990s, selling over 10 million albums worldwide.<ref>{{cite web|first= Bob |last= Grossweiner |first2= Jane |last2= Cohen |title= Gary Cherone Sighting! Extreme Re-Forms |date= November 26, 2007 |website= TicketNews |url= http://www.ticketnews.com/news/Gary-Cherone-Extreme-Re-Forms0110726567 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20140314192654/http://www.ticketnews.com/news/Gary-Cherone-Extreme-Re-Forms0110726567 |archive-date= March 14, 2014}}</ref>

Extreme achieved its greatest success with their second album ''[[Pornograffitti]]'' (1990), which peaked at number 10 on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]], and was certified gold in May 1991 and double platinum in October 1992.<ref>{{cite web|title= Gold & Platinum – Pornograffitti |publisher= [[Recording Industry Association of America]] |access-date= May 16, 2016 |url= https://www.riaa.com/gold-platinum/?tab_active=default-award&ar=&ti=Pornograffitti}}</ref> The album featured the [[Steel-string acoustic guitar|acoustic]] [[ballad]] single "[[More Than Words]]", which reached No. 1 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] in the United States.

==History==
===1985–1989: Formation and debut album===
Extreme was formed in [[Boston]], [[Massachusetts]], in 1985.<ref>{{cite web|first= Stephen Thomas |last= Erlewine |author-link= Stephen Thomas Erlewine |title= Extreme – Artist Biography |publisher= AllMusic |access-date= August 13, 2014 |url= https://www.allmusic.com/artist/extreme-mn0000789064/biography}}</ref> Vocalist Gary Cherone and drummer Paul Geary were in a band together called "Adrenalin" in 1979.  Then they were also members of a band called The Dream, in 1980.  CBS Television bought the rights to the name, "The Dream" for a short lived television series called, "Dreams."  So, they had to rename the band.<ref name="Larkin">{{cite book|editor-first= Colin |editor-last= Larkin |editor-link= Colin Larkin (writer) |date= 1997 |title= [[Encyclopedia of Popular Music|The Virgin Encyclopedia of Popular Music]] |publisher= [[Virgin Books]] |edition= Concise |pages= 444–445 |isbn= 1-85227-745-9}}</ref> Guitarist Nuno Bettencourt was in a band called Sinful, and bassist Pat Badger was playing with a Berklee College-based act called In The Pink. Bettencourt joined Cherone and Geary in a new group in 1985, followed by Badger in 1986. The four chose the name "Extreme" as it sounded like "ex-Dream," a reference to Geary & Cherone's past band, "The Dream."  Gary & Nuno crossed paths numerous times as Gary's brother Mark & Nuno's brother Paulo were in a well known local Boston band together called, "Flesh."

Cherone and Bettencourt began writing songs together and the band performed continuously in the New England area. Extreme grew a large regional following and were named "Outstanding Hard Rock/Heavy Metal Act" at the [[Boston Music Awards]] in 1986 and 1987.

The band had accumulated several original songs by the time A&R director Bryan Huttenhower signed them to [[A&M Records]] in 1987 (which was soon sold to [[PolyGram]] in 1988). The band recorded their [[Extreme (Extreme album)|self-titled debut]] album which was issued in March 1989.<ref name="Larkin"/> The first single was "Kid Ego", a song that Cherone would later admit made him cringe. The final track on the album, "Play with Me", was used as the "mall chase" song in the film ''[[Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure]]''.<ref name="Larkin"/>

===1990–1993: ''Pornograffitti'', ''III Sides to Every Story'', and mainstream success===
Sales of Extreme's first record were sufficient to support a second release. [[Michael Wagener]], who had previously worked with [[Dokken]] and [[White Lion]], was hired to produce the band's ''[[Pornograffitti|Extreme II: Pornograffitti]]'' album in 1990.<ref name="Larkin"/>

The record, which showcased Cherone's lyrics, and Bettencourt's guitar-playing, was a mixture of funk, pop and glam metal sounds. "Decadence Dance" and "[[Get the Funk Out]]" were released as singles. "Get the Funk Out" reached No. 19 in the UK charts in June 1991. Neither single was initially successful in the United States, however, and the album had fallen off the charts when A&M sent the third single to a number of US radio stations.{{citation needed|date=December 2017}}

The [[Steel-string acoustic guitar|acoustic]] [[ballad]] "[[More Than Words]]" entered the [[Billboard Hot 100|Hot 100]] on March 23, 1991, at No. 81. It later became a huge smash, hitting No. 1 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] in the United States.<ref name="Larkin"/> The subsequent single, "[[Hole Hearted]]", another acoustic track, was also successful, rising to No. 4 on the same pop chart.

The band began recording their third album in 1992. Their appearance at [[the Freddie Mercury Tribute Concert]] in April 1992 interrupted the recording sessions, but it gave the band considerable exposure beyond the heavy metal fraternity.<ref name="Larkin"/> By playing a medley at the tribute, as well as "Love of My Life" and "More Than Words" acoustically, Extreme gained a considerable number of fans along with the Queen fan base. At the introductory speech before they played, [[Brian May]] noted that they were "possibly more than any other group on this planet, the people that understand exactly what [[Queen (band)|Queen]] have been about all these years, and what Freddie was about all these years".<ref>{{cite web|first= Eric |last= Garneau |title= A Look Back at the Freddie Mercury Tribute Concert |website= Cover Me |date= November 22, 2011 |access-date= April 30, 2022 |url= https://www.covermesongs.com/2011/11/a-look-back-at-the-freddie-mercury-tribute-concert.html}}</ref>

''[[III Sides to Every Story]]'' was released on September 22, 1992.<ref name="Larkin"/> The first single from the album, "Rest in Peace", had an accompanying video clip inspired by a film short by the [[National Film Board of Canada]] called ''[[Neighbours (1952 film)|Neighbours]]''.<ref>{{cite web|first= Kate |last= Ruscito |title= NFB Remixed : Watch 5 Music Videos Inspired by the NFB |publisher= [[National Film Board of Canada]] |date= June 15, 2015 |access-date= April 30, 2022 |url= https://blog.nfb.ca/blog/2015/06/15/nfb-music/}}</ref>

===1994–1996: Lineup change and ''Waiting for the Punchline''===
Prior to the band's appearance at [[Monsters of Rock|Donington's Monsters of Rock]] festival in the summer of 1994, Geary left the band to pursue a career in artist management. Mike Mangini succeeded him on drums.<ref name="Larkin"/>

''[[Waiting for the Punchline]]'', the first record to feature Mangini on three tracks (Paul Geary played on the rest of the album before departing), was released on February 7, 1995. The singles "[[Hip Today]]", "Unconditionally", and "[[Cynical (song)|Cynical]]" were released, but the album was not a commercial sales success. Extreme disbanded after the tour in 1996, on amicable terms, when Bettencourt decided to leave to pursue a solo career.<ref name="Larkin"/>

===1997–2003: Split and separate projects===
On the recommendation of former Extreme manager [[Ray Danniels]], in 1996, Gary Cherone joined one of the world's most successful rock acts, [[Van Halen]]. During 1996, Van Halen's fan-base weathered the acrimonious departures of two of rock's most successful lead singers: first [[David Lee Roth]], the band's original frontman (1974-1985), and then [[Sammy Hagar]], who had fronted Van Halen since 1985. Into this fractious, and very public, situation entered Cherone, whom guitarist [[Eddie Van Halen]] later called a "musical soulmate".<ref>{{cite web|first= Paul |last= Cantin |title= Report: Van Halen splits with singer |publisher= [[Jam!]]. [[Canoe.ca]] |date= December 1, 2004 |access-date= August 13, 2014 |url= http://jam.canoe.com/Music/Artists/V/Van_Halen/1999/11/05/751518.html |url-status= dead |archive-date= March 10, 2016 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160310163035/http://jam.canoe.com/Music/Artists/V/Van_Halen/1999/11/05/751518.html}}</ref> In 1998, the Cherone-fronted Van Halen released ''[[Van Halen III]]''.

''[[Van Halen III]]'' reached No. 4 on ''Billboard''{{'}}s top 200 album charts, and sold over 500,000 copies in the U.S. alone; however, by Van Halen's standards, it was a failure. All 12 of their previous albums had all sold over two million copies in the U.S. alone, with two selling over ten million in the U.S. alone—and the previous five studio albums had all reached No. 1 on the ''Billboard'' 200 album charts. Van Halen's tour was successful; however, not as successful as in previous years.

In late 1999, after Van Halen's second album with Cherone was "sent back" by [[Warner Bros. Records]],{{citation needed|date=June 2020}} Cherone left the band. He later formed [[Tribe of Judah (band)|Tribe of Judah]], which released an album called ''[[Exit Elvis]]'' in 2002. In 2005, Cherone released a four-song sampler CD, entitled ''Need I Say More''.

In 1997, Nuno Bettencourt released his first solo album titled ''[[Schizophonic (Nuno Bettencourt album)|Schizophonic]]''. In 1998 he formed a group called [[Mourning Widows]] who released a self-titled album that year and a follow-up album, ''[[Furnished Souls for Rent]]'', in 2000. Following the breakup of that band, he released another solo album under the project name of ''Population 1'' in 2002. Acquiring new members for the tour, he decided to keep the name Population 1 and the first release as a band was a five-song EP entitled ''Sessions from Room 4'' in 2004. They then changed the band's name to [[DramaGods]] and created a follow-up CD entitled ''[[Love (DramaGods album)|Love]]'' in 2005. Nuno, along with bandmates [[Kevin Figueiredo]] and Steve Ferlazzo, then went on to collaborate with [[Perry Farrell]]'s project [[Satellite Party]].

''[[The Best of Extreme: An Accidental Collocation of Atoms?]]'', a 13-track Extreme "best-of" collection featuring tracks from the first three studio albums, was released in 1998. ''[[Extreme – The Collection]]'', a later collection including 15-tracks from the first four studio albums, was released in 2002.

===2004–2010: Reformation and ''Saudades de Rock''===
[[File:Extreme - Live Madrid 31 10 2008.jpg|thumb|Bassist [[Pat Badger]] and guitarist [[Nuno Bettencourt]] performing live in 2008. Bettencourt is one of the two constant members of Extreme.]]
Extreme reformed for a short tour in 2004 playing in the [[Azores]] (August), in their hometown of Boston at the [[WKVB (FM)|WAAF]] anniversary (September 19) as well as a few concerts in Japan (January 2005). After a hiatus during 2005, the band returned in 2006 with the "classic" ''Pornograffitti'' lineup (including Paul Geary) to do a small, three-show reunion tour through [[New England]].

In July 2007, Bettencourt quit Satellite Party for another Extreme reunion with Cherone and Pat Badger. On November 26, 2007, the band announced plans for a world tour in the summer of 2008 with [[King's X]] as well as a release date for their new album, ''[[Saudades de Rock]]'', produced by Bettencourt. Kevin Figueiredo, who played with Bettencourt in [[DramaGods]] and Satellite Party, took over drum duties for the band. Original drummer Paul Geary would still remain involved with the band, albeit in a management position. Singles from the album have been available on MySpace including "Star". The album was released on July 28, 2008, in France, August 4, 2008, in Europe, and August 12, 2008, in the United States.

The band then embarked on the [[Take Us Alive World Tour]], supported by [[King's X]] in the US and [[Hot Leg]] in the UK, with various other dates in Europe and Asia, through all of 2008. In 2009, the band continued to tour, co-headlining the [[East Meets West Tour]] with [[Ratt]]. The final date of this tour, in their hometown of Boston, Massachusetts, was recorded for the release of the band's first live DVD called ''[[Take Us Alive]]''.

===2010–2015: Hiatus, Hurtsmile, and other projects===
According to a December 2010 interview with Cherone, Extreme had been writing new material for a new album, which they planned - at the time - to release in 2011. Asked in the same interview if the band will produce the new album by themselves or get an outside producer, Cherone replied, "There's talk of a few people. It would be great to get an A-list name. I don't know if that happens. My dream producer would probably be [[Rick Rubin]]. Here's a guy that's done [[Johnny Cash]], the [[Red Hot Chili Peppers|Chili Peppers]], and, you know, [[Neil Diamond]]."<ref>{{cite web|title= GARY CHERONE Talks EXTREME, VAN HALEN And HURTSMILE in New Interview |website= [[Blabbermouth.net]] |date= December 26, 2010 |access-date= August 13, 2014 |url= http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/gary-cherone-talks-extreme-van-halen-and-hurtsmile-in-new-interview/}}</ref> But due to conflicting schedules with Bettencourt supporting [[Rihanna]] on her tour during 2011, plans to go into the studio were postponed to 2012.

Also in 2010 rumors started about possible commemorative shows for ''Extreme II: Pornograffitti'', given the 20th anniversary of the record. Finally, in 2012, initially a small string of such shows in Japan had been confirmed, marking the full return of the band's activities after a hiatus when Bettencourt was on tour with Rihanna, as well as other side projects by other members, most notably Cherone's [[Hurtsmile]]. Extreme were to tour Australia in April 2013, with [[Richie Kotzen]] as support act, but the shows were cancelled due to scheduling conflicts with Rihanna's 2013 North American tour. They then did their first show in Singapore.

===2015–present: ''Six''===

In a May 2015 interview with Eddie Trunk, vocalist Gary Cherone said that Extreme had been writing and demoing new material for their follow-up to ''Saudades de Rock'', and would enter the studio in the fall to begin recording.<ref>{{cite web|title= Extreme to Record New Music in the Fall, Says Gary Cherone |website= [[Blabbermouth.net]] |date= May 16, 2015 |access-date= May 16, 2015 |url= http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/extreme-to-record-new-music-in-the-fall-says-gary-cherone/}}</ref>

In a September 2016 interview, guitarist Nuno Bettencourt revealed that Extreme had been working on approximately 17 songs for their new album, and added, "We're about 17 songs into it. We're just wrapping them up. We've got to do vocals, some guitar. Slowly but surely." He also stated that the album was expected to be released in early 2017;<ref>{{cite web|title= EXTREME Is Working on 17 Songs for Next Studio Album, Says NUNO BETTENCOURT |website= Blabbermouth.net |date= September 11, 2016 |access-date= September 11, 2016 |url= http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/extreme-is-working-on-17-songs-for-next-studio-album-says-nuno-bettencourt/}}</ref> however, this did not come to fruition and there had been no updates on the album until mid-2022, when Cherone reiterated the album's slow progress in an interview with Eddie Trunk, and described the songs as "some of the best stuff Nuno and [he] have written."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/news/general_music_news/extreme_are_working_on_new_music_announces_frontman_gary_cherone.html|title=Extreme Are Working on New Music, Announces Frontman Gary Cherone|publisher=[[Ultimate Guitar]]|access-date=July 1, 2022|date=July 1, 2022}}</ref>
[[File:Extreme (band) Pat Badger and Kevin Figueiredo Southpark Festival, Finland, 2015.jpg|thumb|Extreme performing in 2015]]
In 2016, the band released ''Pornograffitti Live 25: Metal Meltdown'', an audio/video presentation of its 2015 concert at Las Vegas' Hard Rock Casino.

During the 2017 KISS Kruise, the band invited original drummer Paul Geary to join them on stage to play "Hole Hearted".

In June 2018, Extreme toured Australia with [[Mr. Big (American band)|Mr. Big]], which marked the latter's first tour of Australia and Extreme's first tour of the continent since 1993. After their Australian tour, they went on to tour Kuala Lumpur, Singapore, Bangkok and Taipei.

Extreme headlined Shirock 2019 alongside Scottish hard rock band [[Nazareth (band)|Nazareth]]. On October 19, 2019, the band performed in India in front of over 30,000 fans in [[Ukhrul]].

On February 17, 2023, the band began to release a different teaser each day, to end on February 28. On March 1, 2023, Extreme released the single "Rise" and announced that ''[[Six (Extreme album)|Six]]'' would be released on June 9 of the same year. On April 19, 2023, Extreme released the official videos for "Banshee" and "#Rebel" on their YouTube channel.

==Band members==

'''Current members'''
* [[Gary Cherone]] – lead vocals (1985–1996, 2004, 2005, 2006, 2007–present)
* [[Nuno Bettencourt]] – guitars, keyboards, piano, backing and lead vocals, brass and orchestration arrangements (1985–1996, 2004, 2005, 2006, 2007–present)
* [[Pat Badger]] – bass, backing vocals (1985–1996, 2006, 2007–present)
* [[Kevin Figueiredo]] – drums, percussion (2007–present)

'''Former members'''
* [[Paul Geary]] – drums, percussion, occasional backing vocals (1985–1994, 2004, 2005–2006; special guest 2017)
* [[Mike Mangini]] – drums, percussion (1994–1996, 2004; special guest for three shows in 2006)
* [[Carl Restivo]] – bass, backing vocals (2004)
* [[Steve Ferlazzo]] – keyboards (2004)
* Laurent Duval – bass, backing vocals (2005)
