=== Upcoming twentieth studio album (2024–present) ===
In a February 2024 interview with Audio Ink Radio, guitarist [[Richie Faulkner]] was asked if Judas Priest had "many more albums left" in them. His reply was, "I know personally, whenever we kind of put the writing sessions to bed and we finish the writing and everything, I always feel spent. I'm out of ideas. I've got nothing left, I've given everything to it. Where the hell am I gonna get more ideas from if we choose to do another record? But somehow they always, over the next couple of years, you start banking new riffs and melodies and stuff, and somehow you get a new ones. So you never know what the future holds."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/will-judas-priest-make-any-more-albums-after-invincible-shield-richie-faulkner-responds|title=Will Judas Priest Make Any More Albums After 'Invincible Shield'? Richie Faulkner Responds|website=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=1 March 2024|access-date=2 March 2024}}</ref> When commenting on the possibility of a twentieth studio album, Halford said that "it's inevitable there will be something else."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/rob-halford-says-its-inevitable-that-there-will-be-another-judas-priest-studio-album|title=Rob Halford Says It's 'Inevitable' That There Will Be Another Judas Priest Studio Album|website=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=16 September 2024|access-date=18 September 2024}}</ref>

In an October 2024 interview with [[KBUE#KNAC|KNAC.com]], Faulkner was asked if Judas Priest were going to continue touring in 2025 or planning to hit the studio to write and record another album. His reply was, "I think a bit of both, really. These tours tend to grow and evolve over time — the more we do, we get more offers from different territories and stuff — so I'm sure there'll be more touring. And there's always ideas coming up, there's always creative juices flowing. So if we're able, we might be able to get in and put some ideas together and see where we are. Is there another record? I know we've got ideas coming up all the time — riffs and melodies and song ideas and stuff. We're creative people — as a group of creative people, that's gonna happen. So I think, hopefully if we get some time early next year, we'll be able to pool those ideas and see what we've got and then hopefully hit the road again somewhere else."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/richie-faulkner-weve-got-ideas-coming-up-all-the-time-for-new-judas-priest-music|title=Richie Faulkner: 'We've Got Ideas Coming Up All The Time' For New Judas Priest Music|website=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=3 November 2024|access-date=3 November 2024}}</ref>

In a March 2025 interview with PowerOfMetal.cl, Faulkner said that the band began talks regarding the next album; both him and drummer Scott Travis hoping to begin work in 2026.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/richie-faulkner-says-judas-priest-has-already-talked-about-follow-up-to-invincible-shield-well-have-to-wait-and-see|title=RICHIE FAULKNER Says JUDAS PRIEST Has Already Talked About Follow-Up To 'Invincible Shield': 'We'll Have To Wait And See'|website=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=April 2025 |accessdate=1 April 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/scott-travis-judas-priest-hopes-to-work-on-next-album-in-2026|title=SCOTT TRAVIS: JUDAS PRIEST Hopes To Work On Next Album In 2026|website=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=12 April 2025 |accessdate=12 April 2025}}</ref> On 15 March 2025, former drummer Les Binks died at the age of 73.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/former-judas-priest-drummer-les-binks-dies-band-issues-statement|title=Former JUDAS PRIEST Drummer LES BINKS Dies; Band Issues Statement|website=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=15 April 2025 |accessdate=15 April 2025}}</ref>

== Artistry ==
=== Musical style and influences ===
Judas Priest's style has always been rooted in heavy metal, and many of their albums reflect diverse aspects of the genre. Their debut album, ''[[Rocka Rolla]]'' (1974), is primarily rooted in heavy [[blues rock]]. According to Tim Hall of ''[[The Guardian]]'', "The early Judas Priest albums contained an eclectic mix of styles. Out-and-out rockers sat alongside acoustic ballads, the odd quirky cover and ambitious multi-part epics that owed as much to [[Queen (band)|Queen]] as to [[Black Sabbath]]."<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/musicblog/2016/nov/30/judas-priest-10-of-the-best-rob-halford | title=Judas Priest – 10 of the best | work=The Guardian | first=Tim | last=Hall | date=30 November 2016 | access-date=4 September 2025}}</ref>

From their second album, ''[[Sad Wings of Destiny]]'' (1976), through to their fourth, ''[[Stained Class]]'' (1978), the band's style was somewhat [[progressive music|progressive]], with complex guitar passages and poetic lyrics. Songs would often shift in dynamics and tempo, and the music was some of the heaviest of its day. ''[[Sin After Sin]]'' (1977) used a combination of [[double bass drum]] (or "double kick") and rapid 16th-note bass rhythms combined with rapid 16th-note guitar rhythms used by Black Sabbath, [[Venom (band)|Venom]], and [[Motörhead]] that came to define the genre.<ref name=Cope>{{cite book|author=Andrew Laurence Cope|title=Black Sabbath and the Rise of Heavy Metal Music|date=28 January 2013|publisher=[[Ashgate Publishing]]|isbn=978-1-4094-9398-3|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ft-hAgAAQBAJ&q=Dissident%20Aggressor&pg=PT139}}</ref> While the double-bass rhythms used by Judas Priest are generally measured and technical, the song "[[Dissident Aggressor]]" (from ''Sin After Sin'') pushed an increase in "tempo and aggression", which was later adopted by other bands with a much harder-edged approach.<ref name=Cope />

Starting with their fifth album, ''[[Killing Machine]]'' (1978), the band began to incorporate a more commercial, radio-friendly style to their music. ''[[British Steel (album)|British Steel]]'' (1980) has been referred to as the "record that, more than any other, codified what we mean by heavy metal".<ref>{{cite web|last=Wilkinson |first=Roy |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/may/20/judas-priest-rob-halford-british-steel |title=How Judas Priest invented heavy metal |work=The Guardian |date=20 May 2010 |access-date=10 August 2014}}</ref> The lyrics and music were simplified, and this style prevailed up to their seventh album, ''[[Point of Entry]]'' (1981). With their eighth album, ''[[Screaming for Vengeance]]'' (1982), the band incorporated a balance of these two styles. This continued on ''[[Defenders of the Faith]]'' (1984). With the follow-up album, ''[[Turbo (Judas Priest album)|Turbo]]'' (1986), the band incorporated guitar synthesizers into its signature heavy metal sound. On ''[[Ram It Down]]'' (1988), the band retained some of the more commercial qualities of ''Turbo'' but also returned to some of the fast tempo heavy metal found on their earlier works. This fast-tempo style continued with ''[[Painkiller (Judas Priest album)|Painkiller]]'' (1990). ''[[Jugulator]]'' (1997) tried to incorporate some of the 1990s contemporary [[groove metal]] styles. ''[[Demolition (Judas Priest album)|Demolition]]'' (2001) has a more traditional heavy metal sound with [[nu metal]] elements. Following the return of Halford for ''[[Angel of Retribution]]'' and ''[[Nostradamus (album)|Nostradamus]]'', the band returned to the style of its early albums.<ref name="allmusic">{{cite web|last=Erlewine|first=Stephen Thomas|author-link=Stephen Thomas Erlewine|title=Judas Priest {{!}} Biography & History|url=https://www.allmusic.com/artist/judas-priest-mn0000246611/biography|publisher=[[AllMusic]]}}</ref>

Halford listened to and was influenced by [[Little Richard]], [[Elvis Presley]], [[Janis Joplin]], and [[Robert Plant]] as a vocalist. He learned to push to the limits of his vocal abilities by their vocal demonstrations on record.<ref name="mastropolo">{{cite web|url=http://www.rockcellarmagazine.com/2014/08/05/judas-priest-interview-redeemer-of-souls-rob-halford-tipton-faulkner-spinal-tap/#sthash.l0w4o4nf.YhqbnrCM.dpbs|title=Four Decades of Hellfire with Judas Priest (Interview) – Rock Cellar Magazine|date=5 August 2014|website=Rockcellarmagazine.com|first=Frank|last=Mastropolo|access-date=22 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160221154255/http://www.rockcellarmagazine.com/2014/08/05/judas-priest-interview-redeemer-of-souls-rob-halford-tipton-faulkner-spinal-tap/#sthash.l0w4o4nf.YhqbnrCM.dpbs|archive-date=21 February 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He developed a powerful, operatic vocal style with an impressive range from lower throaty growls to ear-piercing high screams with strong [[vibrato]]. He was also a fan of [[Freddie Mercury]], referring to him as his ultimate hero.<ref name="theguardian.com">{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/may/20/judas-priest-rob-halford-british-steel|title=How Judas Priest invented heavy metal|first=Roy|last=Wilkinson|date=20 May 2010|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=22 January 2018}}</ref>

=== Fashion ===
In addition to the sound, Judas Priest are also known for being revolutionary in [[heavy metal fashion]].<ref name="Bukszpan" /> In the band's early years, they dressed in hippie-style 1970s outfits, but as the decade drew to a close, the rise of punk rock made this look outdated, so the band began wearing simplified wardrobes on their 1978 tour. For the 1979 tour, Halford adopted his now-trademark leather-and-studs look, inspired by punk fashion and [[leather culture]]. The rest of the band adopted a similar style which became prominent at the time of their 1978 release, ''Killing Machine''. This style would go on to be adopted by many heavy metal bands in the early 1980s, especially those of the [[new wave of British heavy metal]] and early [[black metal]] movements.<ref>{{cite news |title=Hell Bent for Leather/Killing Machine Info Page| publisher=Judas Priest Info Pages |url=http://members.firstinter.net/markster/KILLINGMACHINE.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070702171452/http://members.firstinter.net/markster/KILLINGMACHINE.html |archive-date=2 July 2007}}</ref> To this day, it is not uncommon to find metal artists and fans sporting such a look at concerts.

In a published quote on the back cover of [[K. K. Downing]]'s autobiography ''Heavy Duty: Days and Nights in Judas Priest'', Downing said that Judas Priest "had a bit of an identity crisis from the beginning. There was always a bit of a question mark about the band's look. To me, it never seemed to say anything—and in the earliest days of our career, I suppose I actually saw that as a good thing."<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/k-k-downing-i-think-judas-priest-had-a-bit-of-an-identity-crisis-from-the-beginning/|title=K.K. DOWNING: 'I Think JUDAS PRIEST Had A Bit Of An Identity Crisis From The Beginning'|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|access-date=16 July 2018}}</ref>

Downing said he was the one who came up with the band's black-leather look back when he first started in the music business: "I had this Heavy Metal attitude inside of me. I had it all of my life. When I got into Judas Priest I knew I had a band that had a great name. I knew we were a great band ... but something was not quite complete. The leather and studs image came along and it all started to complete itself. We had the album cover with the razor blade ... and Heavy Metal was born, mate. I was a youngster and it came to me. Around 1976 is when it happened. The band took to it and got on with it, really."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://classicrockrevisited.com/show_interview.php?id=1284|author=Wright, Jeb|title=K.K. Downing – Wild Nights & Lots of Words!|publisher=classicrockrevisited.com}}</ref>

Although Halford adopted the gay leather fetish wear for the band's look, he stated that he "had no interest in [[S&M]], [[Dominance and submission|domination]] or the whole [[queer]] subcult of leather and chains" because he is a [[Conventional sex|vanilla]] gay man. He feels that fans of the era also did not suspect a homosexual or [[Kink (sexuality)|kink]] subtext in the leather-and-studs look.<ref>{{cite web |website=Rock and Roll Garage |title=Rob Halford recalls why Judas Priest started using leather |first=Rafael |last=Polcaro |date=December 10, 2020 |url=https://rockandrollgarage.com/rob-halford-recalls-why-judas-priest-started-using-leather/ }}</ref> After Halford's [[coming out]] as gay, modern listeners often identify Judas Priest as having queer themes in their lyrics and fashion.<ref>{{cite web |date=August 6, 2019 |website=Kerrang |first=Sam |last=Moore |title=We Need To Talk About The Queerness Of Judas Priest|url=https://www.kerrang.com/we-need-to-talk-about-the-queerness-of-judas-priest }}</ref>

== Legacy and influence==
Judas Priest have influenced a great deal of metal music since the late 1970s. The band's popularity and status as one of the exemplary and influential heavy metal bands has earned them the nickname "Metal Gods" from their [[Metal Gods|song of the same name]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Berelian |first=Essi |title=The Rough Guide to Heavy Metal |year=2005 |publisher=Rough Guides |isbn= 1-84353-415-0 |page=172}}</ref> They were ranked by [[MTV]] as the second "Greatest Metal Band" of all time (after [[Black Sabbath]]), and [[VH1]] named them the 78th greatest artist of all time in 2010.<ref>{{cite web |work=MTVNews.com |title=The Greatest Metal Bands Of All Time – 2. Judas Priest |url=http://www.mtv.com/bands/m/metal/greatest_metal_bands/071406/index3.jhtml |publisher=MTV |date=9 March 2006 |access-date=10 July 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110905065314/http://www.mtv.com/bands/m/metal/greatest_metal_bands/071406/index3.jhtml |archive-date=5 September 2011}}</ref> They were nominated for induction into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 2018, but were passed over despite placing among the top five fan-voted nominees.<ref>{{cite news|author=Blabbermouth |url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/bon-jovi-to-join-rock-and-roll-hall-of-fame-judas-priest-fails-to-make-the-cut/ |title=BON JOVI To Join ROCK AND ROLL HALL OF FAME; JUDAS PRIEST Fails To Make The Cut|work=Blabbermouth |date=13 December 2017|access-date=21 January 2018}}</ref> In May 2022, it was announced that the band were to be among the 2022 inductee class for the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.<ref name=":2" />

The band have sold over 50 million albums,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-12-02 |title=JUDAS PRIEST Celebrates Over 50 Million Album Sales Worldwide |url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/judas-priest-celebrates-over-50-million-album-sales-worldwide |access-date=2023-05-20 |website=BLABBERMOUTH.NET |language=en}}</ref> including eleven top 30 albums in the United Kingdom.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.wearesonylegacy.com/news/jas-priest-story-original-metal-gods |title=Story Original Judas Priest |access-date=11 January 2017}}{{Dead link|date=August 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes}}</ref> In the United States, the band had eleven consecutive albums to be certified [[Music recording certification|gold]], [[RIAA certification|platinum]] or higher by the [[Recording Industry Association of America|RIAA]], starting with 1977's ''[[Sin After Sin]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Home |url=https://www.riaa.com/ |access-date=2024-01-06 |website=RIAA |language=en-US}}</ref>

Several metal bands have named themselves after classic era Judas Priest songs and albums, including [[Sinner (band)|Sinner]], [[Exciter (band)|Exciter]], [[Running Wild (band)|Running Wild]], [[Steeler (American band)|Steeler]] and Tyrant.

==Awards, nominations, and critical reception==
Despite their huge, loyal fanbase, Judas Priest have never been well-received by much of the music press, partially because their late 1970s rise coincided with the [[punk rock]] and [[new wave music|new wave]] movements, which occupied much of the music press's attention at the time. The first edition of ''[[The Rolling Stone Album Guide]]'' gave their first three albums one star each and described the band as "for lovers of stolen [[Led Zeppelin]] riffs only". The second edition of the guide a few years later also panned their entire discography. ''[[Village Voice]]'' critic [[Robert Christgau]] was notably disdainful of the band, refusing to outright review any of their albums and relegating them to his "Meltdown" list (referring to artists he did not consider having any material worth listening to). In 2018, they were nominated for the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]], but not inducted.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/judas-priests-rob-halford-on-rock-and-roll-hall-of-fame-we-just-want-to-see-some-more-metal-in-there/|title=JUDAS PRIEST's ROB HALFORD On ROCK AND ROLL HALL OF FAME: 'We Just Want To See Some More Metal In There'|date=25 March 2018}}</ref> In the same year, they were inducted into the Hall of Heavy Metal History at the [[Wacken Open Air|Wacken festival]]. Founder/CEO Pat Gesualdo thanked them "for the decades of hard work and dedication to heavy metal, an art form they helped establish." The band then stated that their induction "also sends a great message of inclusion for the metal community around the world, and keeps us defending the metal faith together."<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/video-judas-priest-inducted-into-hall-of-heavy-metal-history-at-germanys-wacken-open-air-festival/|title=Video: JUDAS PRIEST Inducted Into 'Hall Of Heavy Metal History' At Germany's WACKEN OPEN AIR Festival|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|access-date=6 August 2018}}</ref> In 2022, the band was finally inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as the recipients of the committee-selected "Award for Musical Excellence".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rockhall.com/judas-priest-0|title=Rock Hall 2022 Nominee : Judas Priest|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220203065632/https://www.rockhall.com/judas-priest-0 |access-date=14 July 2024|archive-date=3 February 2022 }}</ref> Despite this, many outlets, including [[MetalSucks]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.metalsucks.net/2022/05/04/judas-priest-arent-among-the-2022-rock-and-roll-hall-of-fame-inductees-but-will-receive-the-musical-excellence-award/ |title=Judas Priest Won't Get Inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, but Will Receive the 'Musical Excellence Award'|website=Metalsucks.net |date=4 May 2022}}</ref> and ''[[Loudwire]]'',<ref name="loudwire.com">{{cite web |url=https://loudwire.com/judas-priest-rock-hall-of-fame-musical-excellence-award/ |title=Opinion: Rock Hall Inducting Judas Priest for 'Musical Excellence' is Actually a Backhanded Compliment |website=[[Loudwire]]|date=4 May 2022 }}</ref> were critical of the band being inducted via the "Award for Musical Excellence" rather than in the "Performer" category. Halford, after originally expressing excitement about the honour,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/its-official-judas-priest-to-be-inducted-into-rock-and-roll-hall-of-fame |title=It's Official: JUDAS PRIEST to be Inducted into ROCK AND ROLL HALL OF FAME |date=4 May 2022}}</ref> shared this sentiment.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://metalinjection.net/news/rob-halford-isnt-thrilled-about-judas-priests-rock-hall-induction-via-the-musical-excellence-award |title=ROB HALFORD Isn't Thrilled About JUDAS PRIEST's Rock Hall Induction Via the Musical Excellence Award |date=27 July 2022}}</ref>

== In popular culture ==
The American director [[Rob Reiner]] went to see Judas Priest in concert as part of his preparation for making the film ''[[This Is Spinal Tap]]'' (1984), which spoofs British heavy metal bands.<ref name="mastropolo" />

The drama-comedy film ''[[Rock Star (2001 film)|Rock Star]]'' (2001), starring [[Mark Wahlberg]], is loosely based on the story of how Tim "Ripper" Owens replaced Rob Halford as the vocalist in Judas Priest.

On 5 January 2014, the band appeared in the episode "[[Steal This Episode]]" of comedy cartoon show ''[[The Simpsons]]'' playing a parody of their song "[[Breaking the Law]]". Their music was referred to as "[[death metal]]",<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/jan/14/simpsons-apologise-judas-priest-death-metal|date=14 January 2014|access-date=27 January 2014|first=Ben|last=Beaumont-Thomas|title=The Simpsons apologise to Judas Priest for calling them 'death metal'|work=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> for which the producers subsequently apologised by having [[Bart Simpson]] write "Judas Priest is not 'Death Metal{{'"}} in the opening sequence [[chalkboard gag]].<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/movie-news/bart-simpson-apologizes-for-calling-judas-priest-death-metal-99510/ |title=Bart Simpson Apologizes for Calling Judas Priest 'Death Metal' |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |date=13 January 2014 |access-date=7 December 2019}}</ref>

In 2025, a voice over recording made by [[Toronto|Toronto's]] WILDsound Film Festival contained a quietly read set of unknown song lyrics directly written for [[Rob Halford]] and Judas Priest titled "Dark Elder".<ref>{{citation |url=https://www.wildsound.ca/videos/dark-elder|title=Poetry Reading: Dark Elder|publisher=WILDsound|date=23 July 2025|access-date=18 August 2025}}</ref>

'''Jet''' are<!-- Don't change "are" to "is"; in Australian English band names are treated as noun plurals. --> an Australian rock band formed in 2001. Founding mainstays are brothers [[Nic Cester|Nic]] (vocals, rhythm guitar, piano) and [[Chris Cester]] (drums, vocals) together with [[Cameron Muncey]] (lead guitar and vocals). They were joined in the following year by [[Mark Wilson (musician)|Mark Wilson]] (bass guitar). The quartet released three studio albums ''[[Get Born]]'' (2003), ''[[Shine On (Jet album)|Shine On]]'' (2006) and ''[[Shaka Rock]]'' (2009) before disbanding in 2012. ''Get Born'' is their highest charting work, which peaked at number&nbsp;one in [[ARIA Charts|Australia]], top&nbsp;20 in the United Kingdom and top&nbsp;30 in the United States. Its lead single "[[Are You Gonna Be My Girl]]" (2003) reached the top&nbsp;20 in Australia and UK and top&nbsp;30 in the US. Both ''Shine On'' and ''Shaka Rock'' are Australian top&nbsp;five albums, while their other top&nbsp;20 singles are "[[Look What You've Done]]" (2004), "[[Put Your Money Where Your Mouth Is (song)|Put Your Money Where Your Mouth Is]]" (2006) and "[[She's a Genius]]" (2009).

At the [[ARIA Music Awards of 2004]] they headed the leader board with six&nbsp;wins: [[ARIA Award for Album of the Year|Album of the Year]], [[ARIA Award for Best Group|Best Group]], [[ARIA Award for Best Rock Album|Best Rock Album]] and [[ARIA Award for Breakthrough Artist – Album|Breakthrough Artist – Album]] for ''Get Born'' as well as [[ARIA Award for Single of the Year|Single of the Year]] and [[ARIA Award for Breakthrough Artist – Single|Breakthrough Artist – Single]] for "Are You Gonna Be My Girl". At the [[APRA Awards (Australia)|APRA Awards]] that single won Most Performed Australian Work Overseas in [[APRA Music Awards of 2005|2005]], [[APRA Music Awards of 2006|2006]] and [[APRA Music Awards of 2007|2007]]. Jet reformed in 2016 but released no new studio albums and separated again in 2019. They reunited for a second time in 2023 and were inducted into the [[ARIA Hall of Fame]] in November [[2023 ARIA Music Awards|that year]].

==History==
===Formation and ''Dirty Sweet'' (2001–2003)===
[[File:NicCester Chicago04.jpg|thumb|Founding mainstay, [[Nic Cester]] on lead vocals and guitar, 2004]]
The Cester brothers, [[Nic Cester|Nic]] and [[Chris Cester|Chris]], grew up in [[Dingley Village]] and attended [[St Bede's College (Mentone)|St Bede's College, Mentone]], Melbourne.<ref name="McFarlane">{{cite book |last1=McFarlane |first1=Ian |author-link1=Ian McFarlane |last2=Jenkins |first2=Jeff (Foreword) |title=[[Encyclopedia of Australian Rock and Pop|The Encyclopedia of Australian Rock and Pop]] |chapter=Encyclopedia entry for 'Jet' |date=2017 |location=[[Gisborne, Victoria|Gisborne, VIC]] |publisher=Third Stone Press |edition=2nd |pages=245–246 |isbn=978-0-9953856-0-3 }}</ref> They listened to their father John's [[classic rock]] records from the 1960s and 1970s.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6hOdHbs95go | archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211118/6hOdHbs95go| archive-date=2021-11-18 | url-status=live|title=Jet, the early years |publisher=YouTube |date=2009-07-01 |access-date=2012-04-13}}{{cbignore}}</ref> While still at school Nic formed a group by 1995, which [[Cameron Muncey]] joined.<ref name="Nimmervoll">{{cite web |url=http://www.howlspace.com.au/en5/jet/jet.htm |title=Jet |first1=Ed |last1=Nimmervoll |author-link1=Ed Nimmervoll |website=HowlSpace |via=National Library of Australia |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20070829091427/http://www.howlspace.com.au/en5/jet/jet.htm |archive-date=29 August 2007 |access-date=5 October 2023 |url-status=live }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> Jet's influences include the Beatles, the Rolling Stones, the Faces, AC/DC and [[T. Rex (band)|T. Rex]].<ref name="ODonnell">{{Cite book |title=[[100 Best Australian Albums]] |last1=O'Donnell |first1=John |author-link1=John O'Donnell (music journalist) |last2=Creswell |first2=Toby |author-link2=Toby Creswell |last3=Mathieson |first3=Craig |author-link3=Craig Mathieson |publisher=Hardie Grant Books |date=October 2010 |location=[[Prahran, Victoria|Prahran, Vic]] |isbn=978-1-74066-955-9 }}</ref>{{rp|230–231}} According to Nic, Australian [[power pop]] band [[You Am I]] had the biggest influence on their developing musical tastes:{{blockquote|"''[[Hi Fi Way]]'' was the most important album of my generation... I think everyone our age, who played guitar, played You Am I songs for the first time in front of their school assembly... That was the record that made you realise you could be in an Australian band, you didn't have to be a grunge band and you didn't have to be influenced by American bands. It changed everything."<ref name="ODonnell" />{{rp|230–231}}<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/lifestyle/sunday-magazine/wizards-of-oz/story-e6frf039-1111112857646 |title=Wizards of Oz |author=Tiffany Baker |date=21 January 2007 |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |access-date=16 November 2010}}</ref>}}

Nic, on lead vocals and guitar, decided to form a [[garage rock]] band, in 2001, with Muncey on lead guitar and vocals, before Chris joined on drums and vocals.<ref name="McFarlane" /><ref name="Scatena">{{cite news |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231005030032/https://www.smh.com.au/entertainment/music/happy-landings-all-over-the-globe-as-jet-finally-flames-out-20120330-1w37v.html |title=Happy Landings all Over the Globe as Jet Finally Flames Out |first=Dino |last=Scatena |newspaper=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |date=31 March 2012 |access-date=5 October 2023 |url=https://www.smh.com.au/entertainment/music/happy-landings-all-over-the-globe-as-jet-finally-flames-out-20120330-1w37v.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |archive-date=5 October 2023 }}</ref> Bass guitarist Doug Armstrong, who completed the line-up,<ref name="McFarlane" /> had met the Cesters while working at their father's spice factory. The quartet trialled various band names, Mojo Filter, Hi-Fidelity and Duosonic, before settling for Jet in 2002 – from the song of the [[Jet (song)|same name]] (originally by Paul McCartney and Wings).<ref name="McFarlane" /><ref name="Nimmervoll" /> Their early repertoire was cover versions of You Am I songs and "whatever else was going 'round."<ref name="Nimmervoll" /> "Radio Song" from their debut album ''[[Get Born]]'' was written about difficulties they had obtaining recognition at that time.<ref name="Undercover 1">{{cite web |url=http://www.undercover.com.au/reviews/urjetgetborn.html |title=Jet, ''Get Born'' |website=Undercover |via=[[National Library of Australia]] |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20050601043144/http://pandora.nla.gov.au/pan/11299/20050518-0000/www.undercover.com.au/reviews/urjetgetborn.html |archive-date=1 June 2005 |access-date=4 October 2023 |url-status=bot: unknown }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

Jet supported Melbourne punk rock band the Specimens as an opening act at The Duke of Windsor hotel, [[Windsor, Victoria|Windsor]].<ref name="Levin" /><ref name="Aus Story" /> [[Talent manager]] and booking agent Dave Powell was filling-in for the venue's sound engineer,<ref name="Nimmervoll" /> "I realised the singer could actually sing. I was blown away. They had a lot of potential and I didn't have a lot of bands coming through who were like that."<ref name="Levin">{{cite web |url=http://fasterlouder.junkee.com/jet-rise-fall-melbournes-nu-rock-scene/866437/amp.html |title=Jet, and the Rise and Fall of Melbourne's Nu-rock Scene |first1=Darren |last1=Levin |website=[[Junkee Media|FasterLouder]] |date=13 September 2016 |via=National Library of Australia |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20170227195645/http://pandora.nla.gov.au/pan/151586/20170228-0632/fasterlouder.junkee.com/jet-rise-fall-melbournes-nu-rock-scene/866437/amp.html |archive-date=27 February 2017 |access-date=4 October 2023 |url-status=live }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> Powell signed the then-unnamed group to his management firm.<ref name="Nimmervoll" /><ref name="Aus Story">{{cite web |url=http://www.abc.net.au/austory/content/2011/s3199996.htm |title=''Australian Story'' - 25/04/2011: 'In the Jet Stream' - Transcript |website=[[Australian Story]] |date=25 April 2011 |via=[[National Library of Australia]] |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20151128133943/http://pandora.nla.gov.au/pan/31958/20151129-0000/www.abc.net.au/austory/content/2011/s3199996.htm |archive-date=28 November 2015 |access-date=5 October 2023 |url-status=dead }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> Nic recalled, "Duke of Windsor became our headquarters. [Powell] would be taking calls from you know, executives in Los Angeles from the keg room you know, that was his office."<ref name="Aus Story" /> The members had met [[Mark Wilson (musician)|Mark Wilson]] in 2002 during his performance at that same venue and asked him to replace Armstrong on bass guitar.<ref name="McFarlane" /><ref name="Nimmervoll" /><ref name="Ca$inos Bio" /> Wilson had been in a [[Geelong]]-based band, the Ca$inos.<ref name="Ca$inos Bio">{{cite web |url=http://www.musicaustralia.org/apps/MA?function=showDetail&currentMapsRecord=NAMO~275&itemSeq=10&total=44&returnFunction=searchResults&simpleTerm=Computer+music. |title=Ca$inos |website=[[Music Australia (online resource)|Music Australia]] |date=14 November 2004 |via=National Library of Australia |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20050718173247/http://www.musicaustralia.org/apps/MA?function=showDetail&currentMapsRecord=NAMO~275&itemSeq=10&total=44&returnFunction=searchResults&simpleTerm=Computer+music. |archive-date=18 July 2005 |access-date=5 October 2023 |url-status=live }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

Late in 2002 Jet independently issued a four-track debut extended play ''[[Dirty Sweet]]'', with distribution by Rubber Records.<ref name="McFarlane" /><ref name="Nimmervoll" /><ref name="Levin" /> Its initial pressing of 1000&nbsp;copies was sold out.<ref>{{cite web|url={{AllMusic|class=artist|id=p559321|pure_url=yes}}|publisher=[[Allmusic]]|title=Jet|access-date=28 April 2009|first=MacKenzie|last=Wilson}}</ref> An ''[[NME]]'' writer had obtained a copy of the group's single "Take It or Leave It" from ''Dirty Sweet'' and described it as a mixture of the Rolling Stones and AC/DC.<ref name="Levin" /> [[Elektra Records]] executives signed the band for a recording contract and re-released ''Dirty Sweet'' in May 2003.<ref name="McFarlane" /><ref name="Wilson2">{{cite web | url = {{AllMusic|class=album|id=r641739|pure_url=yes}} |title=''Dirty Sweet'' &#91;EP&#93; Jet |last1=Wilson |first1=MacKenzie |publisher=[[AllMusic]] |access-date=12 July 2013 }}</ref>

===''Get Born'' (2003–2005)===
{{Main|Get Born}}
[[File:Chris Cester.jpg|thumb|Founding mainstay drummer [[Chris Cester]], onstage during [[Sound Relief]], 2009]]
Jet entered the [[Sunset Sound Studios]], Los Angeles with [[Dave Sardy]] producing their debut album ''Get Born'' (September 2003).<ref name="McFarlane" /><ref name="Levin" /> Sardy had produced work for [[Marilyn Manson (band)|Marilyn Manson]] and [[the Dandy Warhols]].<ref name="Sardy Creds">{{cite web |url=https://www.allmusic.com/artist/dave-sardy-mn0000787049/credits |title=Dave Sardy {{!}} Credits |publisher=AllMusic |access-date=4 October 2023 }}</ref> The Australian quartet used [[Billy Preston]] on keyboards for two&nbsp;tracks.<ref name="Sendra">{{cite web |url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/get-born-mw0000324759 |title=Jet – ''Get Born'' Album Reviews, Songs & More |first=Tim |last=Sendra |publisher=AllMusic |access-date=4 October 2023 }}</ref> ''Get Born''{{'}}s title references a lyric from Bob Dylan's "[[Subterranean Homesick Blues]]" (1965) "Ah get born, keep warm."<ref name="Nimmervoll" /> It reached number&nbsp;one in [[ARIA Charts|Australia]] and was accredited 8× platinum by [[Australian Recording Industry Association]] (ARIA).<ref name="AUS Charts">{{cite web |url=https://australian-charts.com/showinterpret.asp?interpret=Jet |title=Discography Jet |first=Steffen |last=Hung |publisher=Australian Charts Portal (Hung Medien) |access-date=4 October 2023 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite certification |region=Australia |type=album |certyear=2004 }}</ref> It peaked in the top&nbsp;20 in the UK and top&nbsp;30 in the US,<ref name="UK">{{cite web|url=http://www.zobbel.de/cluk/CLUK_J.HTM |title=Chart Log UK: Candy J. - JX |website=Zobbel.de |access-date=2011-09-14 }}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|url={{BillboardURLbyName|artist=jet|chart=Billboard 200}}|title=Jet Album & Song Chart History: Billboard 200|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=2010-06-13}}</ref> and was certified platinum in both countries by [[British Phonographic Industry]] (BPI) and [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA), respectively.<ref name="BPI">{{cite web|url=http://www.bpi.co.uk/certified-awards.aspx |title=Certified Awards Search |publisher=[[British Phonographic Industry]] |access-date=16 August 2013 |format=To access, enter the keyword "Jet" and choose the "Search by: Artist" option |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130124005813/http://www.bpi.co.uk/certified-awards.aspx |archive-date= 24 January 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.riaa.com/goldandplatinumdata.php?table=SEARCH_RESULTS&artist=Jet&title=GetBorn&format=ALBUM&go=Search&perPage=50|title=RIAA - Gold & Platinum - 13&nbsp;June 2010: Jet certified albums|publisher=Recording Industry Association of America|access-date=2010-06-13}}</ref>

The Rolling Stones offered Jet a support slot on the Australian leg of their 2003 tour.<ref name="McFarlane" /><ref name="Wilson2" /> Including their own headlining tours, the Australian group played more than 200&nbsp;shows during that 2003.<ref name="high">{{cite magazine |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |date=7 April 2004 |title=Jet's High Times |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/artists/jet/articles/story/5939242/jets_high_times |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061022200307/http://www.rollingstone.com/artists/jet/articles/story/5939242/jets_high_times |url-status=dead |archive-date=22 October 2006 |first=Jenny |last=Eliscu |access-date=4 October 2023 }}</ref> ''Get Born''{{'}}s singles "[[Are You Gonna Be My Girl]]" and "[[Rollover DJ]]" were listed at number&nbsp;one and number&nbsp;nineteen, respectively, on the [[Triple J Hottest 100, 2003]]. "Are You Gonna Be My Girl" appeared on the soundtracks for the video games ''[[Madden NFL 2004]]'', ''[[Guitar Hero: On Tour]]'', ''[[Rock Band (video game)|Rock Band]]'', and ''[[Strictly Come Dancing]]''; the 2006 animated film ''[[Flushed Away]]''; the live-action films ''[[Eurotrip]]'' and ''[[What Happens in Vegas]]''; and as part of two major worldwide advertising campaigns for [[Vodafone]] and [[Apple Inc.|Apple's]] iPod and [[iMac]].

"[[Rollover DJ]]" is used on the soundtrack of [[PlayStation 2]] game ''[[Gran Turismo 4]]''. ''Get Born'' also includes the song "Timothy", dedicated to Muncey's deceased brother – due to its sensitive nature the quartet rarely play the track live.<ref>{{cite magazine |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040602192926/http://inmusicwetrust.com/articles/65h04.html |url=http://www.inmusicwetrust.com/articles/65h04.html |title=Interview: Jet: Australian Rock Imports |magazine=In Music We Trust |date=April 2004 |issue=65 |access-date=4 October 2023 |archive-date=2 June 2004 |url-status=live }}</ref> In early 2004, Jet teamed up with [[The Vines (band)|the Vines]] and [[the Living End]] on The Aussie Invasion tour of US. A new Jet song, "Hold On", not included on ''Get Born'', was used on the [[Spider-Man 2 (soundtrack)|''Spider-Man 2'' soundtrack]] that year. TV and film producer [[J. J. Abrams]] contacted them to record a song for the Season 4 of ''[[Alias (TV series)|Alias]]''. "[[Cold Hard Bitch]]" from ''Get Born'' was used, and used during a frenetic scene of two [[Central Intelligence Agency|CIA]] agents sprinting down a [[Hong Kong]] street, giving the band further US exposure.

Later in 2004 Jet received nominations for the annual US [[Radio Music Awards]], including Artist of the Year: Rock Radio, Artist of the Year: Rock Alternative Radio, and Song of the Year: Rock Radio (for "Cold Hard Bitch"). They also received the [[American Music Awards of 2004|32nd Annual American Music Awards]] nomination as Favorite Artist – Alternative Music, as well as three nominations at the [[2004 MTV Video Music Awards]], held in Miami in August. "Are You Gonna Be My Girl" was nominated for [[MTV Video Music Award for Best Rock Video|Best Rock Video]], [[MTV Video Music Award for Best New Artist|Best New Artist]] and [[MTV Video Music Award for Best Editing|Best Editing]] in a video. Jet performed "Are You Gonna Be My Girl" live at the ceremony and picked up the award for Best Rock Video,<ref name="MTV Won">{{cite news |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210609145443/http://www.smh.com.au/entertainment/music/jet-win-mtv-award-20040830-gdjnby.html |title=Jet Win MTV Award |newspaper=The Sydney Morning Herald |date=30 August 2004 |access-date=5 October 2023 |url=http://www.smh.com.au/entertainment/music/jet-win-mtv-award-20040830-gdjnby.html |url-access=subscription |archive-date=9 June 2021 }}</ref> dedicating it to the Cesters' late father.

Following their success in the US, back home the group headed the leader board at the [[ARIA Music Awards of 2004]] by winning six categories: [[ARIA Award for Album of the Year|Album of the Year]], [[ARIA Award for Best Group|Best Group]], [[ARIA Award for Best Rock Album|Best Rock Album]] and [[ARIA Award for Breakthrough Artist – Album|Breakthrough Artist – Album]] for ''Get Born'' as well as [[ARIA Award for Single of the Year|Single of the Year]] and [[ARIA Award for Breakthrough Artist – Single|Breakthrough Artist – Single]] for "Are You Gonna Be My Girl". They were also nominated for [[ARIA Award for Highest-Selling Album|Highest-Selling Album]]. At the ceremony in October the quartet performed "Are You Gonna Be My Girl";<ref name="Donovan" /> while Nic provided lead vocals on a cover version of Stevie Wright's "[[Evie (song)#The Wrights version|Evie (part 1)]]" as a member of an Australian super-group [[The Wrights (Australian band)|the Wrights]], with Spiderbait's [[Kram (musician)|Kram]] (drums), the Living End's [[Chris Cheney]] (guitar), [[Dallas Crane]]'s Pat Bourke (bass guitar) and You Am I's [[David Lane (musician)|Davey Lane]] (guitar).<ref name="Cashmere">{{cite web |url=http://www.undercover.com.au/news/2005/jan05/20050107_wrights.html |title=Nic Cester Supergroup Christened the Wrights |first1=Paul |last1=Cashmere |author-link1=Paul Cashemere |website=Undercover |date=7 January 2005 |via=National Library of Australia |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20051118034940/http://pandora.nla.gov.au/pan/11299/20051118-0000/www.undercover.com.au/news/2005/jan05/20050107_wrights.html |archive-date=18 November 2005 |access-date=5 October 2023 |url-status=bot: unknown }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> ''Get Born''{{'}}s "[[Look What You've Done]]" (No.&nbsp;24) and "Get What You Need" (No.&nbsp;89) were listed on the [[Triple J Hottest 100, 2004]].<ref name="Triple J 2004">{{cite web |url=https://www.abc.net.au/triplej/hottest100/archive/search/?year=2004 |title=Search {{!}} Hottest 100 Archive: 2004 |date=11 November 2017 |publisher=Triple J (Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC)) |access-date=7 October 2023 }}</ref>

During a show at the [[MCG]] in October 2005, Nic declared that he considered his group to be "up there with the greatests, with fucking [[John Lennon|Lennon]] and the Stones." This caused controversy but was settled when Australian music magazines began publishing articles comparing Jet's albums with those of famous 1960s and 1970s bands.<ref name="Schuler">{{cite magazine |last=Schuler |first=Rachel |date=3 November 2014 |title=Where Are They Now: Jet |url=http://www.infectiousmagazine.com/where-are-they-now-jet/ |magazine=Infectious Magazine |location=Australia |access-date=6 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150327102521/http://www.infectiousmagazine.com/where-are-they-now-jet/ |archive-date=27 March 2015 }}</ref> ''Get Born'' is listed at No.&nbsp;89 in the book, ''[[100 Best Australian Albums]]'' (October 2010).<ref name="ODonnell" />{{rp|230}} The authors described it as "free of the neurotic self-examination that passes for meaningful songwriting in the post-Nirvana era."<ref name="ODonnell" />{{rp|230}}

===''Shine On'' (2006–2008)===
[[File:Mark Wilson (musician) jet 2004.jpg|thumb|[[Mark Wilson (musician)|Mark Wilson]] on bass guitar (centre), March 2004]]
"[[Put Your Money Where Your Mouth Is (Jet Song)|Put Your Money Where Your Mouth Is]]" was released to radio as a single in August 2006 ahead of their second album, ''[[Shine On (Jet album)|Shine On]]''. It followed on 30 September (2 October in the UK, 3 October in the US) with a physical listing of 15&nbsp;tracks. An extra track, "Coming Home Soon", was available only from the ITunes Store. ''Shine On'' debuted at No.&nbsp;3 on the Australian charts and was accredited platinum by ARIA in 2006.<ref name="AUS Charts" /><ref>{{Cite certification |region=Australia |type=album |certyear=2008 }}</ref> Critical reaction to the album was mixed,<ref name="McFarlane" /> with British music magazine ''[[NME]]''{{'}}s Paul McNamee calling it "another joyfully old-fashioned rock'n'roll album immersed in the classics."<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.nme.com/reviews/jet/8037 |title=Reviews – Jet: ''Shine On'' |first1=Paul |last1=McNamee |magazine=[[NME]] |date=29 September 2006 |access-date=5 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061124082900/https://www.nme.com/reviews/jet/8037 |archive-date=24 November 2006 }}</ref> US music blogger Ray Suzuki of ''[[Pitchfork Media|Pitchfork]]'' gave the album 0.0 out of 10 and posted a video of a chimpanzee urinating in its own mouth instead of a written review.<ref name="McFarlane" /><ref>{{cite web |url=https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/9464-shine-on/ |title=Jet: ''Shine On'' |first1=Ray |last1=Suzuki |website=[[Pitchfork Media|Pitchfork]] |date=2 October 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231001115352/https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/9464-shine-on/ |archive-date=1 October 2023 }}</ref> "Put Your Money Where Your Mouth Is" appeared on the "[[Chuck (TV series)|Chuck]]" TV series pilot episode, "[[Chuck Versus the Intersect]]". It also was added to a compilation CD, ''NME: The Essential Bands – Festival Edition''.

Jet played at the [[MTV Europe]] Awards in [[Copenhagen]] in early November 2006.<ref name="MTV 2006k">{{cite web |url=https://www.gettyimages.co.uk/detail/news-photo/nic-cester-and-jet-perform-on-stage-during-the-13th-annual-news-photo/72353431 |title=Nic Cester and Jet Perform on Stage During the 13th Annual MTV Europe... News Photo |website=Getty Images |date=2 November 2006 |access-date=5 October 2023 }}</ref> It was their first live performance since Nic's [[laryngitis]] halted their World Tour early in the previous month.<ref name="Tijs">{{cite web |url=http://undercover.com.au/News-Storyf756.html |title=Jet Postpones Rest of European Tour |first1=Andrew |last1=Tijs |website=Undercover |date=18 October 2006 |via=National Library of Australia |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20100517222859/http://pandora.nla.gov.au/pan/11299/20100518-0000/undercover.com.au/News-Storyf756.html |archive-date=17 May 2010 |access-date=5 October 2023 |url-status=live }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> In mid-November Jet returned to Australia and performed at the [[Make Poverty History Concert]] at [[Sidney Myer Music Bowl]], Melbourne.<ref name="Make Poverty">{{cite web |url=http://www.yourgigs.com.au/news/index.cfm?i=110248 |title=Jet Adds Shine to Make Poverty History |website=yourGigs.com.au |date=13 November 2006 |via=National Library of Australia |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20070903074941/http://www.yourgigs.com.au/news/index.cfm?i=110248 |archive-date=3 September 2007 |access-date=5 October 2023 |url-status=live }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> They also held a show on a barge floating on the [[Yarra River]].<ref name="Boud">{{cite web |url=http://www.boudist.com/archive/2006/11/23/photographing-jet.html |title=Photographing Jet |first1=Daniel |last1=Boud |website=Boudist Photos |date=13 November 2006 |via=National Library of Australia |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20110512174854/http://pandora.nla.gov.au/pan/58813/20110512-0856/www.boudist.com/archive/2006/11/23/photographing-jet.html |archive-date=12 May 2011 |access-date=5 October 2023 |url-status=bot: unknown }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> The performance was broadcast via Triple J's radio programme ''[[Live at the Wireless]]''.<ref name="tranzfusion.net">{{cite web |url=https://tranzfusion.net/music/news/2006/The-Great-Australian-Music-Quiz-and-Jet-live/ |title=The Great Australian Music Quiz and Jet live |website=tranzfusion.net |date=17 November 2006 |access-date=5 October 2023 }}</ref>

The next singles from ''Shine On'', "[[Bring It On Back]]" (in the UK) and "[[Rip It Up (Jet song)|Rip It Up]]" (in Australia) appeared in late 2006. The album provided a five-track EP, also titled ''Shine On'', which was issued in December. The title track, "[[Shine On (Jet song)|Shine On]]", was released on various dates in March 2007 as a single. It is a tribute to the Cesters' father, who had died of cancer in 2004.<ref name="Donovan">{{cite news |url=http://www.theage.com.au/articles/2004/10/17/1097951560187.html |title=Jet Dominate the ARIAs |first1=Patrick |last1=Donovan |newspaper=[[The Age]] |date=18 October 2004 |access-date=6 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071013091309/http://www.theage.com.au/articles/2004/10/17/1097951560187.html |archive-date=13 October 2007 }}</ref> The track was written by Nic from the perspective of his father encouraging those who outlived him to "shine on". Other songs on the album ("Come On Come On", "Bring It On Back", "Stand Up", "Holiday", "All You Have to Do") deal with overcoming adversity and challenge. ''Shine On''{{'}}s "Put Your Money Where Your Mouth Is" (No.&nbsp;72) and "Rip It Up" (No.&nbsp;76) were listed on the [[Triple J Hottest 100, 2006]].<ref name="Triple J 2006">{{cite web |url=https://www.abc.net.au/triplej/hottest100/archive/search/?year=2006 |title=Search {{!}} Hottest 100 Archive: 2006 |date=11 November 2017 |publisher=Triple J (Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC)) |access-date=7 October 2023 }}</ref>

Jet co-headlined the 2007 [[Big Day Out]] festivals in Australia and New Zealand, alongside fellow headliners [[Tool (band)|Tool]], [[Muse (band)|Muse]], [[the Killers]], and [[My Chemical Romance]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.inthemix.com.au/news/aust/28762/Big_Day_Out_lineup_announced_for_real |title=Big Day Out 2007 Lineup |first1=Tim |last1=Hardaker |website=Inthemix.com.au |date=3 October 2006 |access-date=5 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061022221501/http://www.inthemix.com.au/news/aust/28762/Big_Day_Out_lineup_announced_for_real |archive-date=22 October 2006 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Also in that year, they released "Falling Star" for the [[Spider-Man 3 (soundtrack)|''Spider-Man 3'' soundtrack]],<ref name="Girl.com 1">{{cite web |url=http://www.girl.com.au/spiderman3-soundtrack.htm |title=''Spiderman 3'' & Soundtrack |website=Girl.com.au |date=23 December 2010 |via=National Library of Australia |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20101223084209/http://www.girl.com.au/spiderman3-soundtrack.htm |archive-date=23 December 2010 |access-date=5 October 2023 |url-status=live }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> while "Rip It Up" appeared on the ''[[TMNT (film)|TMNT]]'' soundtrack,<ref name="TMNT ST">{{Citation | title=Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Music from the Motion Picture |date=2007 |publisher=Atlantic Recording |url=https://trove.nla.gov.au/work/200777059 |access-date=5 October 2023}}</ref> which also was the official theme for the wrestling show ''WWE''{{'}}s 2010 ''[[SummerSlam]]''.<ref name="dailymotion">{{cite web |url=https://www.dailymotion.com/video/xe3o9v |title=SummerSlam 2010 Theme Song 'Rip It Up'[HD] - Video |work=Dailymotion |date= |access-date=5 October 2023 }}</ref> In June and August, they supported the Rolling Stones on the European leg of their [[A Bigger Bang (concert tour)|A Bigger Bang]] World Tour in Lisbon,<ref name="iorr.org 1">{{cite web |url=https://iorr.org/tour05/lisbon.htm |title=The Rolling Stones Lisbon Portugal show 2007 |work=IORR |date=25 June 2007 |access-date=5 October 2023 }}</ref> Madrid and London ([[The O2 Arena|O2 Arena]]).<ref name="iorr.org 2">{{cite web |url=https://iorr.org/tour05/madrid.htm |title=The Rolling Stones Madrid Spain show 2007 |work=IORR |date=28 June 2007 |access-date=5 October 2023 }}</ref><ref name="iorr.org 3">{{cite web |url=https://iorr.org/tour05/london4.htm |title=The Rolling Stones O2 #2 Arena London UK show 2007 |work=IORR |date=23 August 2007 |access-date=5 October 2023 }}</ref>

In October 2007 the band returned to Australia to perform at the [[AFL Grand Final]] and to finish the rest of their world tour.<ref name="McFarlane" /> In November the members announced they would take "some time off" as they needed "down time".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://thelondonpaper.typepad.com/thelondonblog/2007/10/jet-split-for-n.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071027065431/http://thelondonpaper.typepad.com/thelondonblog/2007/10/jet-split-for-n.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=27 October 2007 |title=Jet split... for now |work=The London Blog }}</ref> On 24 October Chris and Wilson produced a song "[[I Spy I Spy]]", under the moniker the Vice Lords, for the [[Japan]]ese former duo [[Superfly (band)|Superfly]]. They collaborated with [[Iggy Pop]] to release a joint rendition of [[Johnny O'Keefe]]'s single "[[Wild One (Johnny O'Keefe_song)#Jet and Iggy Pop version|Wild One]]" as "The Wild One – A Tribute to Johnny O'Keefe" on its 50th anniversary in July 2008.<ref name="ARIA Report 961">{{cite journal |date=28 July 2008 |title= Week Commencing ~ 11th May 2009 ~ Issue #961 |last1=Wallace |first1=Ian |journal=The ARIA Report |publisher=[[Australian Recording Industry Association]] (ARIA) |issue=961 |pages=2, 4, 7, 12, 15 }}</ref><ref name="Cashmere 2">{{cite web |url=http://undercover.com.au/News-Storye6e5.html |title=Iggy Pop and Jet to Go Wild at Hall of Fame |first1=Paul |last1=Cashmere |website=Undercover |date=27 April 2008 |via=National Library of Australia |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20090517232203/http://pandora.nla.gov.au/pan/11299/20090518-0000/undercover.com.au/News-Storye6e5.html |archive-date=17 May 2009 |access-date=6 October 2023 |url-status=live }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> It also appeared on the compilation and tribute album of the same name later that year.<ref name="NLA Wild">{{Citation |last1=O'Keefe |first1=Johnny |author-link1=Johnny O'Keefe |title=The Wild One |date=2008 |publisher=[[Warner Music Australia]] |url=https://trove.nla.gov.au/work/34111419 |access-date=6 October 2023}}</ref>

===''Shaka Rock'' and disbandment (2009–2012)===
[[File:Jet as the opening act of an Oasis Concert. - 42838413 05.jpg|thumb|Jet performing live (2004)]]
In a video on their website band members talked about writing and recording songs at Atlantic Sound Studios in New York City; Chris quipped: "We've got to stop writing; we got too many songs." Jet returned to Australia to play a show in Melbourne on 17 December to debut new material, "Goodbye Hollywood", "Walk", "Start the Show", "Black Hearts", "She's a Genius", "Seventeen", and "Beat On Repeat". Muncey expressed that he "really, really loves the song 'Seventeen'... I think is sort of a step forward for us songwriting-wise. It's sorta got everything wrapped into one, a storyline, and sad to say melancholy. It's rock and roll, it's rocking, it's got all these other albums to it, you know, so I find it really interesting."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mtvasia.com/News/200908/20018356.html |title=Jet: Shaking Up the Airwaves with ''Shaka Rock'' |first1=Daryl |last1=Tan |date=20 August 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090827123732/http://www.mtvasia.com/News/200908/20018356.html |archive-date=27 August 2009 }}</ref>

Jet played at [[Melbourne Cricket Ground]] and [[Sydney Cricket Ground]] on 14 March 2009 for [[Sound Relief]], which was a multi-venue rock music concert in support of relief for the [[Black Saturday bushfires|Victorian Bushfire Crisis]].<ref name="Brumby">{{cite web|url=http://www.premier.vic.gov.au/premier/artists-unite-for-sound-relief-bushfire-benefit.html |title=Artists Unite for 'Sound Relief' Bushfire Benefit - Premier of Victoria, Australia |last=Brumby |first=John |author-link=John Brumby |publisher=Premier of Victoria |date=24 February 2009 |access-date=2009-02-25 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090716020126/http://www.premier.vic.gov.au/premier/artists-unite-for-sound-relief-bushfire-benefit.html |archive-date=16 July 2009 }}</ref><ref name="Mitchell">{{cite news|url=http://www.news.com.au/heraldsun/story/0,21985,25099180-661,00.html |title=Coldplay, Kings of Leon to headline bushfire Relief Concerts |last=Mitchell |first=Geraldine |series=[[Herald Sun]] |work=[[The Herald and Weekly Times]] |date=24 February 2009 |access-date=2009-02-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090227120155/http://www.news.com.au/heraldsun/story/0%2C21985%2C25099180-661%2C00.html |archive-date=27 February 2009 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The Melbourne event was held simultaneously with a concert at the Sydney Cricket Ground.<ref name="Brumby"/> All the proceeds from the Melbourne Concert went to the [[Red Cross]] Victorian Bushfire relief.<ref name="Brumby"/><ref name="Mitchell"/><ref name="Official">{{cite web|url=http://www.soundrelief.com.au/melb/index.php|title=Latest News|publisher=Sound Relief|access-date=2009-02-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090227073309/http://www.soundrelief.com.au/melb/index.php |archive-date=2009-02-27}}</ref> Half the proceeds from the Sydney concert went to the Victorian Bushfire relief and the other half for [[Queensland]] [[Flood]] relief.<ref name="Brumby"/><ref name="Mitchell"/> Appearing with Jet in Sydney were [[Coldplay]], [[Eskimo Joe]], [[Hoodoo Gurus]], [[Icehouse (band)|Icehouse]], [[Josh Pyke]], [[Little Birdy]], [[the Presets]], [[Wolfmother]], You Am I and additional artists.<ref name="Official"/> Jet and Wolfmother were the only groups to perform at both venues.

Jet's song, "She's a Genius" from ''[[Shaka Rock]]'', appeared on a ''NCIS'' Season 7 Episode 2 – "Reunion". In April 2009, "K.I.A (Killed in Action)" was made available on the band's official website.<ref name="Official"/> It was the 5th most added song to radio in Australia.<ref>[http://www.themusicnetwork.com.au/20.0.html] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070103203909/http://www.themusicnetwork.com.au/20.0.html|date=3 January 2007}}</ref> "[[She's a Genius]]", the first single from the album, was issued in June 2009. ''Shaka Rock'' appeared Australia on 21 August 2009, which peaked at number&nbsp;five and was accredited platinum by ARIA in 2019.<ref name="AUS Charts" /><ref>{{Cite certification |region=Australia |type=album |certyear=2019 }}</ref>

"Black Hearts (On Fire)" was released as its second single in November 2009 with a music video provided. "Black Hearts" also appeared in the Australian film adaptation of ''[[Tomorrow, When the War Began]]''. In November 2009 ''She's a Genius'' was certified Gold by ARIA for shipment of more than 35,000 copies.<ref>{{Cite certification |region=Australia |type=single |certyear=2009 }}</ref> "Timothy (Where Have You Been)" was used on the album ''[[Shock Value II]]'' by US record producer [[Timbaland]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.timbalandmusic.com/discography/default.aspx?pid=2447|title=Timbaland : Album : Shock Value 2|publisher=timbalandmusic.com|access-date=2013-03-08|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130321125617/http://www.timbalandmusic.com/discography/default.aspx?pid=2447|archive-date=21 March 2013}}</ref> In December the quartet were the support act for [[punk rock]] trio [[Green Day]] on the Australian leg of their [[21st Century Breakdown World Tour]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.triplem.com.au/melbourne/music/news//blog/jet-support-green-day/20091118-6ivm.html |title=Jet support Green Day |publisher=Triplem.com.au |access-date=2011-09-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120314022916/http://www.triplem.com.au/melbourne/music/news/blog/jet-support-green-day/20091118-6ivm.html |archive-date=2012-03-14}}</ref> ''Shaka Rock''{{'}}s "She's a Genius" (No.&nbsp;77) was listed on the [[Triple J Hottest 100, 2009]].<ref name="Triple J 2009">{{cite web |url=https://www.abc.net.au/triplej/hottest100/archive/search/?year=2009 |title=Search {{!}} Hottest 100 Archive: 2009 |date=11 November 2017 |publisher=Triple J (Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC)) |access-date=7 October 2023 }}</ref>

"Seventeen" was issued as the third single in April 2010, which reached No.&nbsp;31 and was certified gold by ARIA.<ref>{{Cite certification |region=Australia |type=single |certyear=2010 }}</ref> During that month the group appeared on TV variety show ''[[Hey Hey It's Saturday]]''{{'}}s first episode since the reunion series, for performances of "She's a Genius" and "Seventeen".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Fr5ckuTHaFE | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151019102005/http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Fr5ckuTHaFE| archive-date=2015-10-19 | url-status=dead|title=Jet on Hey Hey It's Saturday |publisher=Youtube.com |access-date=2011-09-14}}</ref> From September to November 2010 the rock quartet toured Australia as the support act for Powderfinger's [[Sunsets Farewell Tour]].<ref>[http://www.powderfinger.com/sunsetstour] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100412062930/http://www.powderfinger.com/sunsetstour|date=12 April 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mtv.com.au/events/e2192d4a-powderfinger-sunsets-tour/|title=Powderfinger's Final Tour!|publisher=[[MTV Australia]]|access-date=2011-09-14|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120306030033/http://www.mtv.com.au/events/e2192d4a-powderfinger-sunsets-tour/|archive-date=6 March 2012}}</ref> While Nic and Muncey were on a hiatus from performing, in early 2011 Wilson on bass guitar and Chris on lead vocals formed a doom-disco band, the DamnDogs, in Los Angeles with Louis Macklin on keyboards and electronics and Mitch McIvor (Cesters' cousin) on guitar.<ref name="Scatena" /><ref name="Tijs 2">{{cite web |url=http://www.undercover.fm/news/15050-jet-members-post-new-music-as-damn-dogs.html |title=Jet Members Post New Music as Damn Dogs |first1=Andrew |last1=Tijs |website=Undercover |date=9 June 2011 |via=National Library of Australia |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20150516183506/http://pandora.nla.gov.au/pan/11299/20150517-0001/www.undercover.fm/news/15050-jet-members-post-new-music-as-damn-dogs.html |archive-date=16 May 2015 |access-date=7 October 2023 |url-status=usurped }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref name="Heath">{{cite web |url=http://www.theaureview.com/sydney/damn-dogs-wolf-cub-oxford-art-factory-21-07-11.html |title=DamnDogs + Wolf & Cub - Oxford Art Factory (21.07.11) |first1=Larry |last1=Heath |website=the AU review |date=24 July 2011 |via=National Library of Australia |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20120108222703/http://pandora.nla.gov.au/pan/128344/20120108-0000/www.theaureview.com/sydney/damn-dogs-wolf-cub-oxford-art-factory-21-07-11.html |archive-date=8 January 2012 |access-date=7 October 2023 |url-status=bot: unknown }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> They released a debut EP ''Strange Behaviour'' on 9 August 2011 via iTunes. On 26 March 2012 Jet announced their "discontinuation as a group," via their official website and Facebook:<ref name="Scatena" />
{{blockquote|"A Message to Our Fans: After many successful years of writing, recording and touring we wish to announce our discontinuation as a group. From the many pubs, theatres, stadiums and festivals all across the world it was the fans that made our amazing story possible and we wish to thank them all. Thank you, and goodnight."<ref name="Jet Gone">{{cite web | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120919225107/http://jettheband.com/news/67961 | url = http://jettheband.com/news/67961 | title = A Message to Our Fans | publisher = Jet Official Website | date = 26 March 2012 | archive-date = 19 September 2012 | access-date = 15 August 2014 }}</ref>}}

According to ''Infectious Magazine''{{'}}s Rachel Schuler, "Later it was stated that personal issues and arguments were the reason for the split."<ref name="Schuler" />

===Reformations and upcoming fourth album (2016–present)===
Jet members announced in September 2016 that they would reform in the following year and were due to open five shows for [[Bruce Springsteen]] and the [[E Street Band]] on the latter's "[[The River Tour 2016#Oceanic leg/Summer '17 tour|Summer '17]]" tour in February 2017.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://musicfeeds.com.au/news/jet-just-totally-stoked-reunion-rumours-big-time/ |title=Jet Just Totally Stoked Those Reunion Rumours Big Time |first1=Emmy |last1=Mack |date=11 September 2016 |newspaper=Music Feeds |access-date=6 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161230002549/http://musicfeeds.com.au/news/jet-just-totally-stoked-reunion-rumours-big-time/ |archive-date=30 December 2016 }}</ref><ref name="Williams">{{cite web |url=http://musicfeeds.com.au/news/jet-frontman-nic-cester-release-debut-solo-album-2017/ |title=Jet Frontman Nic Cester to Release Debut Solo Album In 2017 |first1=Tom |last1=Williams |website=Music Feeds |date=22 February 2017 |via=National Library of Australia |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20180421233609/http://musicfeeds.com.au/news/jet-frontman-nic-cester-release-debut-solo-album-2017/ |archive-date=21 April 2018 |access-date=7 October 2023 |url-status=live }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> In October 2016 they announced on social media that their first headline show in 6&nbsp;years was due at Sydney's [[Taronga Zoo]] also in February 2017.<ref name="Williams" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/jettheband/app/123966167614127/|title=Jet – Tour Dates {{!}} Facebook|website=www.facebook.com|access-date=2016-12-29}}</ref> For the performance they were joined on stage by Macklin on keyboards and the Wolfgramm Sisters on backing vocals.<ref name="Young">{{cite web |url=http://thebrag.com/jet-taronga-zoo/amp/index.html |title=Jet @ Taronga Zoo |first1=David James |last1=Young |website=The Brag |date=20 February 2017 |via=National Library of Australia |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20190615055919/http://pandora.nla.gov.au/pan/169055/20190615-0055/thebrag.com/jet-taronga-zoo/amp/index.html |archive-date=15 June 2019 |access-date=6 October 2023 |url-status=live }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> The show subsequently sold out, so a second one was added.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.facebook.com/jettheband/posts/10154780372429704:0 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/facebook/33476194703/10154780372429704 |archive-date=2022-02-26 |url-access=limited |title=Jet – Sydney! WildHoney & Bloods will be joining us at... {{!}} Facebook |website=www.facebook.com |access-date=2016-12-29}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Jet had made their official live return at a one-off headlining show at Melbourne's Gasometer Hotel on 31 January 2017. They performed with Macklin and played a 23&nbsp;song set-list, which drew from all three of studio albums.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.setlist.fm/setlist/jet/2017/the-gasometer-hotel-melbourne-australia-4bf82b3e.html|title=Jet Concert Setlist at The Gasometer Hotel, Melbourne on January 31, 2017|publisher=Setlist.FM|date=31 January 2017|access-date=2 February 2017}}</ref>

While living in [[Italy]], Nic had been invited by Simone Cogo ({{abbr|p.k.a.|performer known as}} [[the Bloody Beetroots]] or DJ Bob Rifo) to collaborate on "My Name Is Thunder".<ref name="Cashmere 3" /> Once Nic's band mates were appraised they joined the project, which was issued as a single in July 2017.<ref name="Cashmere 3">{{cite web |url=http://www.noise11.com/news/jet-the-bloody-beetroots-release-my-name-is-thunder-20170710.html |title=Jet + the Bloody Beetroots Release 'My Name Is Thunder' |first1=Paul |last1=Cashmere |website=Noise11.com |date=10 July 2017 |via=National Library of Australia |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20200909003852/http://pandora.nla.gov.au/pan/178078/20200909-0000/www.noise11.com/news/jet-the-bloody-beetroots-release-my-name-is-thunder-20170710.html |archive-date=9 September 2020 |access-date=6 October 2023 |url-status=bot: unknown }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> The track is the Australian rock group's first new song in seven&nbsp;years.<ref name="John">{{cite web |url=http://tonedeaf.com.au/jet-just-released-first-song-in-seven-years/amp/index.html |title=Jet Just Released Their First Song in 7 Years, and It's Definitely not What We Were Expecting |first1=Brandon |last1=John |website=[[Luke Girgis#Brag Media|Tone Deaf]] |date=7 July 2017 |via=National Library of Australia |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20170724110203/http://pandora.nla.gov.au/pan/152679/20170724-0850/tonedeaf.com.au/jet-just-released-first-song-in-seven-years/amp/index.html |archive-date=24 July 2017 |access-date=6 October 2023 |url-status=live }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> It also appeared on the Italian artist's album, ''The Great Electronic Swindle'' (October 2017), Rifo reflected, "we had different ideas on the mixing and from that, we came up with two versions. It's the best of both our worlds!"<ref name="Cashmere 3" /><ref name="John" />

In 2018 the quartet announced their 15th anniversary Australian national tour for ''Get Born'', with dates in Newcastle, Sydney, Canberra, Brisbane, Perth, Adelaide and Melbourne. They issued their first live album ''Get Born: Live at the Forum'' in May to commemorate that tour.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Williams |first1=Tom |title=Jet Announce 2018 'Get Re-Born' 15th Anniversary National Tour |url=http://musicfeeds.com.au/news/jet-announce-2018-get-re-born-15th-anniversary-national-tour/ |website=Music Feeds |access-date=6 October 2023 |date=13 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231005010759/https://musicfeeds.com.au/news/jet-announce-2018-get-re-born-15th-anniversary-national-tour/ |archive-date=5 October 2023 }}</ref> They made a brief UK visit, playing in Manchester and London. They supported [[Jimmy Barnes]] alongside Eskimo Joe in 2019,<ref>{{cite web |title=Jimmy Barnes, Jet and Eskimo Joe to Tour the Country in 2019 |url=https://www.abc.net.au/doublej/music-reads/music-news/jimmy-barnes-jet-eskimo-joe-tour-2019/11137218 |date=22 May 2019 |publisher=[[Double J (radio station)|Double J]] ([[Australian Broadcasting Corporation]] (ABC)) |access-date=20 June 2022}}</ref> and played their final show of their reunion at the By The C open-air concert in [[Coffs Harbour]] on 26 October 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jet Setlist at Park Beach Reserve, Coffs Harbour, Australia |url=https://www.setlist.fm/setlist/jet/2019/park-beach-reserve-coffs-harbour-australia-3b9d3874.html |website=Setlist.FM |access-date=20 June 2022}}</ref>

Nic then resumed his solo career, releasing an album, ''The Skipping Girl'', in 2021. It was a companion to his first children's book of the same name.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rose |first1=Anna |title=Jet's Nic Cester to Release Children's Book and Accompanying Album, 'Skipping Girl' |url=https://www.nme.com/en_au/news/music/jets-nic-cester-to-release-childrens-book-and-accompanying-album-skipping-girl-3085860 |website=NME Australia |date=3 November 2021 |access-date=20 June 2022}}</ref> Nic as a member of a supergroup [[the Jaded Hearts Club]] had issued ''You've Always Been Here'' in October 2020.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Shutler |first1=Ali |title=The Jaded Hearts Club – ''You've Always Been Here'' Review: Well-intentioned but Often Unlistenable Dad-Rock |url=https://www.nme.com/en_au/reviews/album/the-jaded-hearts-club-youve-always-been-here-review-2767923 |website=NME |date=2 October 2020 |publisher=BandLab Technologies |access-date=20 June 2022}}</ref> Wilson performed as a member of the Australian Rock Collective (or ARC), which included Kram, Powderfinger's [[Darren Middleton]] and Davey Lane. ARC perform tribute shows of classic albums, such as the Beatles' ''[[Let It Be (album)|Let It Be]]'' and Neil Young's ''[[Harvest (Neil Young album)|Harvest]]''.<ref>{{cite web |last1=de la Couer |first1=Sidonie Bird |title=ARC to pay homage to Neil Young and The Beatles at the Palais Theatre |url=https://beat.com.au/arc-to-pay-homage-to-neil-young-and-the-beatles-at-the-palais-theatre/ |website=Beat Magazine |date=27 April 2022 |access-date=20 June 2022}}</ref>

At the end of 2022 Nic was interviewed on a podcast and revealed Jet were in talks to reunite in the studio. "Next year is the 20 year anniversary of the release of the first Jet album. We're actually in discussions right now, sharing musical ideas for the first time with the idea of maybe trying to release some new material next year. This is just as of 3 weeks ago, so we'll see if it happens or not. It's looking good so far."<ref>{{cite web |title=Nachts Um Halb 1 – The Music Podcast in 3D Audio |url=https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/nachts-um-halb-1-der-musikpodcast-in-3d-audio/id1622205718?i=1000589777875 |access-date=18 December 2022 }}</ref> In June 2023 the quartet officially announced their reunion and shared Australian tour dates for that September where they would perform ''Get Born'' in its entirety.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Varvaris |first1=Mary |title=Jet Announce 'Get Born' 20th Anniversary Australian Tour |url=https://themusic.com.au/news/jet-announce-get-born-20th-anniversary-australian-tour/N_qFKyotLC8/14-06-23 |website=theMusic.com.au | date=14 June 2023 |access-date=14 June 2023}}</ref><ref name="Lochrie">{{cite magazine |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230614000508/https://au.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/jet-get-born-20th-anniversary-tour-tickets-47896/l/jet-get-born-20th-anniversary-tour/ |title=Jet ''Get Born'' 20th Anniversary Tour |first=Conor |last=Lochrie |magazine=Rolling Stone Australia |date=14 June 2023 |access-date=6 October 2023 |url=https://au.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/jet-get-born-20th-anniversary-tour-tickets-47896/l/jet-get-born-20th-anniversary-tour/ |archive-date=14 June 2023 |url-status=live }}</ref> Shortly before the tour began, they announced that Los Angeles resident Chris would not be joining the tour due to a family emergency.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Varvaris |first1=Mary |title=Jet Drummer Chris Cester Won't Be Joining the Band's Australian Tour |url=https://themusic.com.au/news/jet-drummer-chris-cester-won-t-be-joining-the-band-s-australian-tour/7h5M4OPi5eQ/14-09-23 |website=theMusic.com.au |publisher=SCG Media |access-date=6 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231004051150/https://themusic.com.au/news/jet-drummer-chris-cester-won-t-be-joining-the-band-s-australian-tour/7h5M4OPi5eQ/14-09-23 |archive-date=4 October 2023 |url-status=live }}</ref> Macklin had returned as touring keyboardist, while Pete Marin took on drums in place of Chris.<ref name="Chin">{{cite web |url=https://www.lilithia.net/jet-20th-anniversary-tour-melbourne-2023/ |title=Jet: 20th Anniversary Tour, Forum Melbourne, Melbourne, September 22nd 2023 – Live Review |first= |last= |website=Lilithia Reviews |date=23 September 2023 |access-date=6 October 2023 }}</ref><ref name="Lockheart">{{cite web |url=https://scenestr.com.au/music/review-jet-hindley-street-music-hall-adelaide-20230925 |title=Review: Jet @ Hindley Street Music Hall (Adelaide) |first=Mike |last=Lockheart |website=scenestr.com.au |date=25 September 2023 |access-date=6 October 2023 }}</ref> Jet were inducted into the [[ARIA Hall of Fame]] at the [[2023 ARIA Music Awards]] in November.<ref name="LeFevre">{{cite web |last1=LeFevre |first1=Jules |title=Jet to Be Inducted into the ARIA Hall of Fame |url=https://musicfeeds.com.au/news/jet-aria-hall-of-fame/ |website=Music Feeds |date=19 September 2023 |publisher=Evolve Media |access-date=21 September 2023}}</ref><ref name="NME 1">{{cite web |url=https://www.nme.com/en_au/news/music/aria-awards-2023-winners-list-3539653 |title=ARIA Awards 2023: the Nominees & Winners as They're Announced |website=[[NME|NME Australia]] |date=15 November 2023 |access-date=17 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116052203/https://www.nme.com/en_au/news/music/aria-awards-2023-winners-list-3539653 |archive-date=16 November 2023 |url-status=live }}</ref> At the ceremony they performed a medley of their hits, "Cold Hard Bitch", "Look What You've Done" and "Are You Gonna Be My Girl".<ref name="Brandle 2023">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/awards/troye-sivan-dmas-taylor-swift-2023-aria-awards-1235471303/ |title=2023 ARIA Awards: Troye Sivan Wins Big |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |first=Lars |last=Brandle |date=15 November 2023 |access-date=17 November 2023 }}</ref><ref name="Anderson 2">{{cite web |url=https://www.popsugar.com.au/celebrity/aria-awards-biggest-moments-2023 |title=The 2023 ARIA Awards Biggest Moments |first=Stephanie |last=Anderson |website=PopSugar Australia |date=16 November 2023 |access-date=17 November 2023 }}</ref>

In April 2024, Jet announced that after 15 years, they had started work on a new album, tentatively due for release in 2025. The band also announced a limited edition 7-inch vinyl record containing the new song "Hurry Hurry", which was released in May. A music video for "Hurry Hurry" was released in September 2024.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ETT36M7_zs8 |title=Jet - Hurry Hurry (Official Video) |date=2024-09-05 |last=Jet |access-date=2024-09-17 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

==Activism==
In 2007 Jet members joined a public campaign by [[People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals]] (PETA), which called for an end to [[Seal hunting#Canada|Canada's annual seal hunt]].<ref name="Eliezer">{{cite web |url=http://www.themusic.com.au/imm_display7f3d.html |title=Christie Eliezer's Music Business News |first1=Christie |last1=Eliezer |website=In Music & Media |date=22 May 2007 |via=National Library of Australia |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20090218024857/http://pandora.nla.gov.au/pan/10761/20090218-0018/www.themusic.com.au/imm_display7f3d.html |archive-date=18 February 2009 |access-date=6 October 2023 |url-status=bot: unknown }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> The petition was signed by some 150,000 names, which included fellow Australian musicians [[John Butler (musician)|John Butler]], members of [[Something for Kate]], [[Red Riders]] and the Vines.<ref name="Eliezer" />

===The Fred Hollows Foundation===
In May 2008, Jet released a video clip on [[YouTube]], which is tribute to the work of the late [[Fred Hollows]] and The Fred Hollows Foundation.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://hollows.org |title=The Fred Hollows Foundation|website=Hollows.org}}</ref> Nic highlighted Hollow's work to restore sight to people blinded by [[cataract]]s in developing countries, which was ongoing 15&nbsp;years after his death. "Hollows was such a big figure in Australia and he had a huge impact, but he passed away when there was still work to do," Cester said in a statement. "This clip is a bit of a reminder, hopefully it encourages people to make a donation to keep [Hollow]'s work going."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.ninemsn.com.au/article.aspx?id=569559 |title=Jet Releasing Fred Hollows Tribute Clip (Nine-MSN) |publisher=News.ninemsn.com.au |access-date=2011-09-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090112091123/http://news.ninemsn.com.au/article.aspx?id=569559 |archive-date=2009-01-12}}</ref> The video tribute uses Jet's song "Shine On" along with images compiled by [[The Fred Hollows Foundation]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://optuszoo.news.ninemsn.com.au/article.aspx?id=569559 |title=Jet releasing Fred Hollows tribute clip (Nine-MSN) |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090112083805/http://optuszoo.news.ninemsn.com.au/article.aspx?id=569559 |archive-date=2009-01-12}}</ref>
